Unde dictum est alibi: Factus est obediens usque ad mortem, propter quod et Deus exaltavit illum; et in Psalmo, De torrente in via bibet, propterea exaltabit caput. Ideo autem modico quam angeli minoratus est, id est mortalis effectus, assumendo naturam passibilem, ut gratia Dei, id est non humanis meritis, sed gratuita Dei voluntate et pia liberalitate, pro omnibus gustaret mortem, id est, pro universorum salute, quantum in se est, mortis amaritudinem experiretur. Unde et Propheta: Dominus (inquit) posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum. Pro solis tamen electis passus est Christus, quantum ad efficaciam, prout ait: Venit Filius hominis dare animam suam redemptionem pro multis.
paras.en: But him [[2:9|who was made a little lower than the angels|qui modico quam angelis minoratus est]], that is, who was made less than the angels in a small degree, namely as to the passibility of his body. […] *nam*, that is, made lower, […] [[2:9|for the suffering of death|passionem mortis]], that is, by the merit of his deadly passion, which brought death upon him, [[2:9|crowned with glory and honour|gloria et honore coronatum]], as has been explained. Hence it is said elsewhere: He became [[Phil 2:8|obedient unto death|Factus est obediens usque ad mortem]]: [[Phil 2:9|For which cause, God also hath exalted him|propter quod et Deus exaltavit illum]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 109:7|He shall drink of the torrent in the way: therefore shall he lift up the head|De torrente in via bibet, propterea exaltabit caput]]. And he was [[2:9|made a little lower than the angels|modico quam angeli minoratus est]] for this reason, that is, made mortal by taking a passible nature: [[2:9|that, through the grace of God|ut gratia Dei]], that is, not by human merits but by the free will and loving liberality of God, [[2:9|he might taste death for all|pro omnibus gustaret mortem]], that is, that he might experience the bitterness of death for the salvation of all, as far as lay in him. Hence the Prophet too: [[Is 53:6|the Lord|Dominus]], he says, [[Is 53:6|hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum]]. Yet Christ suffered for the elect alone as to efficacy, as he says: [[Matt 20:28|the Son of man|Venit Filius hominis]] came [[Matt 20:28|to give his life a redemption for many|dare animam suam redemptionem pro multis]].

paras.t: Decebat enim eum, propter quem omnia et per quem omnia: id est, conveniens erat Deo Patri, propter quem omnia facta sunt ab ipso, sicut propter causam finalem (omnia enim propter se ipsum operatus est Dominus), et per quem omnia, id est, a quo omnia facta sunt, sicut ex causa efficiente; vel, Per quem, sicut per causam exemplarem; qui multos filios adoptivos, videlicet homines electos, in gloriam adduxerat, id est, ad æternam beatitudinem perducere præordinavit in sua prædestinatione æterna; auctorem salutis eorum, id est Christum electorum salvatorem, qui eis salutem promeruit sua passione dignissima, per passionem consummare, id est per mortem crucis ab hac vita tollere, exponendo videlicet, imo tradendo eum morti crucis pro nostra redemptione; vel, Per passionem consummare, id est ad finem seu consummationem nostræ liberationis, merito passionis adducere. Convenientissimus quippe modus humanæ redemptionis fuit, quod Pater Unigenitum suum humana natura vestivit, et morti pro hominum salvatione exposuit: quia per hoc maxime commendatur bonitas et misericordia ejus, qua miseris et aliunde seductis tam clementer subvenit; justitia quoque, quoniam peccata hominum non reliquit inulta. Nulla etiam pura creatura digna erat pro hominibus satisfacere: tanta est enormitas culpæ per comparationem ad Deum, et dignitas vitæ æternæ consistentis in Deo, sicut in immediato objecto. Decuit etiam eamdem naturam pati in Salvatore, quæ erat in salvandis reparanda.
paras.en: [[2:10|For it became him|Decebat enim eum]], [[2:10|for whom are all things and by whom are all things|propter quem omnia et per quem omnia]]: that is, it was fitting for God the Father, for whom all things were made by him, as for their final cause (for [[Prov 16:4|The Lord hath made all things for himself|omnia enim propter se ipsum operatus est Dominus]]), and by whom are all things, that is, by whom all things were made, as by their efficient cause; or, by whom, as by their exemplar cause; [[2:10|who had brought many children|qui multos filios]] by adoption, namely elect men, [[2:10|into glory|in gloriam adduxerat]], that is, foreordained in his eternal predestination to lead them to eternal beatitude; [[2:10|the author of their salvation|auctorem salutis eorum]], that is, Christ, the saviour of the elect, who merited salvation for them by his most worthy passion, [[2:10|to perfect|consummare]] [[2:10|by his passion|per passionem]] [*consummare*, "to perfect", is also "to bring to an end"], that is, to take him from this life by the death of the cross, namely by exposing him, or rather handing him over, to the death of the cross for our redemption; or, [[2:10|to perfect|consummare]] [[2:10|by his passion|per passionem]], that is, to bring to its end or completion our deliverance by the merit of his passion. For the most fitting way of man's redemption was this, that the Father clothed his Only-begotten with human nature and exposed him to death for the salvation of men: because by this above all his goodness and mercy are commended[[Rom 5:8||]][[Rom 5:9||]], with which he came so mercifully to the help of the wretched, who had been led astray by another; and his justice too, since he did not leave the sins of men unpunished. Moreover, no mere creature was worthy to make satisfaction for men: so great is the enormity of sin in comparison with God, and the dignity of eternal life, which consists in God as in its immediate object. It was fitting, too, that the same nature should suffer in the Saviour which was to be repaired in those who were to be saved.

paras.t: Quod vero decuit Christum pati, ostendit Apostolus: quoniam decet sanctificatorem et sanctificatos esse ejusdem naturæ, quatenus satisfaciat quod offendit, id est, eadem natura patiendo reformet, quæ male agendo peccavit. Natura ergo humana in primo parente posterisque infecta, per Christi humanitatem fuerat reparanda. Dicit igitur: Qui enim sanctificat, id est Christus qui peccatores a vitiis purgat, et qui sanctificantur, id est electi qui merito suæ passionis mundantur, ex uno omnes, id est, ex eodem patre atque principio profluxerunt. Christus nempe secundum assumptam humanitatem, descendit de Adam, sicut et nos: excepta infectione originalis peccati, et quod immediate de Virgine natus est. Secundum divinam vero naturam, natus est ex Patre æterno, de quo et nos nati sumus: difformiter tamen, quoniam ipse est Filius naturalis et unicus, nos autem adoptivi et plurimi.
paras.en: That it was fitting for Christ to suffer, the Apostle shows thus: because it is fitting that the sanctifier and the sanctified should be of the same nature, so that the nature which offended should make satisfaction, that is, so that the same nature should restore by suffering what it had sinned by doing evil. Human nature, then, infected in our first parent and in his descendants, was to be repaired through the humanity of Christ. He says therefore: [[2:11|For both he that sanctifieth|Qui enim sanctificat]], that is, Christ, who cleanses sinners from their vices, [[2:11|and they who are sanctified|et qui sanctificantur]], that is, the elect, who are cleansed by the merit of his passion, [[2:11|are all of one|ex uno omnes]], that is, have come forth from the same father and principle. For Christ according to the humanity he assumed descended from Adam, as we do, except for the infection of original sin, and that he was born immediately of the Virgin. And according to his divine nature he was born of the eternal Father, of whom we too are born: yet not in the same way, since he is the natural and only Son, and we are adopted sons, and many.

paras.t: Propter quam causam, videlicet quoniam Christus et membra ejus, puta fideles, unum paternum principium habent, et in natura communicant: unde et ait in Joanne, Ascendo ad Patrem meum et Patrem vestrum; non confunditur fratres eos vocare, non obstante quod ipse sit Deus verus et homo a peccato immunis, illi vero propter peccatum degeneres, dicens ad Patrem in Psalmo: Nuntiabo nomen tuum fratribus meis, id est, te ipsum et gloriam tuam, o Pater, prædicabo Apostolis aliisque discipulis. De his enim dixit Mariæ Magdalene: Vade et dic fratribus meis. In medio Ecclesiæ primitivæ, videlicet inter fideles primo conversos, laudabo te. Stetit enim Jesus in medio discipulorum suorum: quibus et sæpe apparuit per dies quadraginta, intrans et exiens, et quadam vice plus quam quingentis fratribus apparens. Hæc etiam fecit Salvator ante passionem, quando seorsum discipulis suis disseruit omnia. Potest quoque generaliter de omnibus fidelibus accipi: quibus Christus per Apostolos et successores eorum nomen Patris æterni prædicavit; atque in medio Ecclesiæ, id est ubique in omni congregatione fidelium, eum laudavit, imo et laudat et prædicat.
paras.en: [[2:11|For which cause|Propter quam causam]], namely because Christ and his members, that is, the faithful, have one fatherly principle and share one nature (hence he says in John: [[John 20:17|I ascend to my Father and to your Father|Ascendo ad Patrem meum et Patrem vestrum]]), [[2:11|he is not ashamed to call them brethren|non confunditur fratres eos vocare]], notwithstanding that he is true God, and a man free from sin, while they are degenerate through sin, [[2:11|saying|dicens]] to the Father in the Psalm: [[2:12|I will declare thy name to my brethren|Nuntiabo nomen tuum fratribus meis]], that is, I will preach thee thyself and thy glory, O Father, to the Apostles and the other disciples. For of these he said to Mary Magdalene: [[John 20:17|go to my brethren and say to them|Vade et dic fratribus meis]]. [[2:12|in the midst of the church|In medio Ecclesiæ]] in its beginning, that is, among those first converted to the faith, [[2:12|will I praise thee|laudabo te]]. For Jesus [[John 20:19|stood in the midst|Stetit enim Jesus in medio]] of his disciples[[John 20:26||]], to whom he also appeared often for forty days[[Acts 1:3||]], going in and out, and once appearing to [[1 Cor 15:6|more than five hundred brethren|plus quam quingentis fratribus]]. The Saviour did this also before his passion[[Mark 9:30||]], when [[Mark 4:34|apart, he explained all things to his disciples|seorsum discipulis suis disseruit omnia]] [the margin gives Mark ix, 31 (in our numbering 9:30, where he teaches his disciples apart); Denis's words are those of Mark 4:34]. It can also be taken generally of all the faithful, to whom Christ has preached the name of the eternal Father through the Apostles and their successors; and in the midst of the Church, that is, everywhere in every congregation of the faithful, he has praised him, nay, still praises and preaches him.

paras.t: Et iterum Christus ait per Isaiam, quantum ad sensum, quamvis verba non habeantur in nostra translatione secundum hanc formam: Ego ero fidens in eum, id est, ego Christus secundum quod homo passibilis, sperabo in Deum, non per spem quæ est virtus theologica, quam non habui, sed per quamdam fiduciam qua resurrectionem et corporis glorificationem ab eo certissime exspectavi. Hoc autem Christo non competeret, nisi verus homo fuisset: ideo non confunditur homines vocare fratres. — Et iterum Christus ait: Ecce ego et pueri mei, id est discipuli et spirituales filii mei: quibus et dixit, Pueri, numquid pulmentarium habetis? quos dedit mihi Dominus, id est, per caritatem et gratiam mihi tanquam capiti copulavit, eosque per me salvare decrevit. De talibus dicit in Evangelio: Tui erant, et mihi eos dedisti; itemque: Pater, manifestavi nomen tuum hominibus, quos dedisti mihi de mundo. Ex hoc testimonio patet, quod tam ipsi quam Christus, sint ex uno principio, scilicet Deo. Hanc auctoritatem Isaiæ intelligit Lyra melius hoc loco, quam super Isaiam. Hic namque dicit eam ad litteram de discipulis Christi debere intelligi, ibi vero exponit eam litteraliter de discipulis Isaiæ.
paras.en: [[2:13|And again|Et iterum]] Christ says through Isaias[[Is 8:17||]], as to the sense, although the words are not found in this form in our translation: [[2:13|I will put my trust in him|Ego ero fidens in eum]], that is, I, Christ, as a passible man, will hope in God: not with the hope which is a theological virtue, which I did not have [hope as a theological virtue looks for the vision of God, which the soul of Christ already enjoyed], but with a certain confidence, by which I most surely awaited from him the resurrection and the glorification of my body. This would not befit Christ had he not been true man: and so he is not ashamed to call men brethren. [[2:13|And again|Et iterum]] Christ says: [[2:13|Behold I and my children|Ecce ego et pueri mei]][[Is 8:18||]], that is, my disciples and spiritual sons, to whom he also said: [[John 21:5|Children, have you any meat?|Pueri, numquid pulmentarium habetis?]] [the margin gives John xvi; the words are in John 21:5]; [[2:13|whom God hath given me|quos dedit mihi Dominus]] [Denis reads *Dominus*, "the Lord", as in Isaias, for *Deus*, "God"], that is, whom he has joined to me as to their head by charity and grace, and has decreed to save through me. Of such he says in the Gospel: [[John 17:6|Thine they were: and to me thou gavest them|Tui erant, et mihi eos dedisti]]; and again: Father, [[John 17:6|I have manifested thy name to the men whom thou hast given me out of the world|manifestavi nomen tuum hominibus, quos dedisti mihi de mundo]] [the margin gives John 17:9 for these words, which are in 17:6; 17:9 has "them whom thou hast given me: because they are thine"]. From this testimony it is clear that both they and Christ are of one principle, namely God. Lyra understands this authority of Isaias better in this place than in his commentary on Isaias. For here he says it is to be understood literally of the disciples of Christ, but there he expounds it literally of the disciples of Isaias.

paras.t: Consequenter ostenditur quod decuit Christum incarnari et pati, ex parte salvandorum. Quum ergo pueri, id est fideles electi, communicaverunt carni et sanguini, id est, ex corpore et anima facti sunt, et homines mortales fuerunt, et ipse Christus similiter participavit eisdem, id est, carnem veram et animam rationalem assumpsit, factus mortalis; ut per mortem, id est propriæ passionis merita, destrueret, id est, superaret et foras ejiceret, eum qui habebat mortis imperium, id est diabolum, mortis auctorem, qui homines ad mortem culpæ induxit, ex qua secuta est mors naturæ, et mors secunda, videlicet mors gehennæ. Deus enim mortem non fecit; sed invidia diaboli mors introivit in orbem terrarum. Habuit autem diabolus mortis imperium, quoniam ante Christi adventum, omnes quodammodo in morte detinuit. In libro quoque Sapientiæ dicitur Deus habere imperium vitæ et mortis; et in Apocalypsi ait Salvator: Habeo claves mortis et inferni. Sed Deus dicitur habere mortis imperium, quia quos vult, in morte relinquit, et quos vult, a morte reducit. Non autem inducit mortem culpæ. Christus vero habet claves mortis, hoc est, potestatem relaxandi peccata.
paras.en: Next it is shown that it was fitting for Christ to become incarnate and to suffer, on the part of those who were to be saved. [[2:14|Therefore because the children|Quum ergo pueri]], that is, the elect faithful, [[2:14|are partakers of flesh and blood|communicaverunt carni et sanguini]], that is, were made of body and soul and were mortal men, [[2:14|he also himself|et ipse]], Christ, [[2:14|in like manner hath been partaker of the same|similiter participavit eisdem]], that is, took true flesh and a rational soul, being made mortal: [[2:14|that, through death|ut per mortem]], that is, through the merits of his own passion, [[2:14|he might destroy|destrueret]], that is, overcome and cast out, [[2:14|him who had the empire of death, that is to say, the devil|eum qui habebat mortis imperium, id est diabolum]], the author of death, who led men into the death of sin, from which followed the death of nature and the second death[[Apoc 21:8||]], namely the death of hell [the margin gives Apoc. xxi; the second death is named in 21:8]. For [[Wis 1:13|God made not death|Deus enim mortem non fecit]]; but [[Wis 2:24|by the envy of the devil, death came into the world|invidia diaboli mors introivit in orbem terrarum]]. Now the devil had the empire of death because before the coming of Christ he held all men, in a manner, in death. In the book of Wisdom, too, God is said to have the empire of life and death[[Wis 16:13||]] [the margin gives Wis. xvi; the place is 16:13, which has "power of life and death"]; and in the Apocalypse the Saviour says: I [[Apoc 1:18|have the keys of death and of hell|Habeo claves mortis et inferni]][[Apoc 20:13||]]. But God is said to have the empire of death because those whom he wills he leaves in death, and those whom he wills he brings back from death. He does not, however, bring on the death of sin. And Christ has the keys of death, that is, the power of forgiving sins.

paras.t: Et liberaret Christus sua passione eos qui timore mortis corporalis, per totam vitam obnoxii, id est rei et subditi, erant servituti culpæ ac dæmonis, id est homines universos, qui maluerunt peccare, quam corporalem mortem incurrere, magis timentes eos qui corpus occidunt, quam qui corpus et animam perdere potest in gehennam. Tales erant homines, ut plurimum, ante Christi passionem; sed ipse sua passione præstitit nobis exemplum moriendi pro justitia, et abstulit suis hunc inordinatum timorem. Secundo exponitur specialiter de Judæis: Et liberaret eos, puta Judæos, ab oneribus legis, per gratiam et meritum suæ passionis, qui timore mortis corporalis, quam lex inflixit transgressoribus suis, vel gehennalis, quam lex minabatur, per totam vitam præsentem obnoxii, id est subjecti, servituti legis: nam timore pœnarum potius quam amore justitiæ legem servabant. Christus enim sua passione legem, quantum ad cærimonialia, evacuavit: qua evacuata, fecit Judæos liberos, ut per fidem et gratiam salvarentur sine observantia cærimonialium, ministrarentque Deo amore potius quam timore.
paras.en: [[2:15|And might deliver|Et liberaret]], Christ by his passion, [[2:15|them, who through the fear of death|eos qui timore mortis]] of the body [[2:15|were all their lifetime subject|per totam vitam obnoxii]], that is, guilty and subjected, [[2:15|to servitude|erant servituti]] of sin and of the devil: that is, all men, who chose rather to sin than to incur bodily death, fearing [[Matt 10:28|them that kill the body|eos qui corpus occidunt]] more than [[Matt 10:28|him that can destroy both soul and body in hell|qui corpus et animam perdere potest in gehennam]]. Such, for the most part, were men before the passion of Christ; but he by his passion gave us an example of dying for justice, and took this disordered fear from his own. Secondly, it is expounded specially of the Jews: [[2:15|And might deliver them|Et liberaret eos]], namely the Jews, from the burdens of the law, by the grace and merit of his passion, [[2:15|who through the fear of death|qui timore mortis]] of the body, which the law inflicted on its transgressors, or of hell, with which the law threatened them, [[2:15|were all their lifetime|per totam vitam]] here [[2:15|subject|obnoxii]], that is, subjected, [[2:15|to servitude|servituti]] of the law: for they kept the law from fear of punishment rather than from love of justice. For Christ by his passion made void the law as to its ceremonies[[Eph 2:15||]]; and having made it void, he made the Jews free, so that they might be saved by faith and grace without observing the ceremonies, and might serve God from love rather than from fear.

paras.t: Denique, quod Christus pueris communicavit in carne et sanguine, hominesque redemit, ostendit Apostolus. Nusquam enim angelos apprehendit, id est, nunquam legitur angelos apostatas ad gratiam reduxisse, aut angelicam naturam assumpsisse; sed semen Abrahæ apprehendit, id est, carnem humanam ex semine Abrahæ sibi univit, et populum Judæorum specialiter revocavit: de quibus locutus est, Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel.
paras.en: Lastly, the Apostle shows that Christ shared flesh and blood with the children and redeemed men. [[2:16|For nowhere doth he take hold of the angels|Nusquam enim angelos apprehendit]], that is, we nowhere read that he brought the apostate angels back to grace, or that he took on the angelic nature; [[2:16|but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold|sed semen Abrahæ apprehendit]], that is, he united to himself human flesh from the seed of Abraham, and called back the Jewish people in particular, of whom he said: [[Matt 15:24|I was not sent but to the sheep, that are lost of the house of Israel|Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel]].

paras.t: Unde, id est propter hanc causam, videlicet quia semen Abrahæ apprehendit, debuit, debito condecentiæ, non obligationis, per omnia, id est in omnibus naturalibus proprietatibus atque defectibus indetrahibilibus, fratribus, id est ceteris hominibus, similari, non autem in defectibus detrahibilibus, scilicet in culpa et defectu necessariorum. Non enim debuit esse claudus, cæcus, aut languidus, quamvis tempore passionis elanguit. Fuit ergo aliis similis, quia mortalis, uberibus lactatus, crevit, esuriit, manducavit, mortem perpessus est. Ut misericors fieret, id est misericordiam impertiret; vel, Misericors fieret actu et habitu in natura humana, qui æternaliter misericors est in natura divina; et fidelis pontifex, id est verus mediator atque sacerdos pro nobis, ad Deum Patrem vel Trinitatem, immolando se ipsum Deo in cruce hostiam immaculatam in odorem suavitatis; ut repropitiaret, id est, Deum placando deleret, delicta populi, id est totius generis humani: sicut dicit Joannes, Ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris. De hoc pontifice ait quoque Petrus: Conversi estis ad pastorem et episcopum animarum vestrarum.
paras.en: [[2:17|Wherefore|Unde]], that is, for this reason, namely because he took hold of the seed of Abraham, [[2:17|it behoved him|debuit]], by a debt of fittingness, not of obligation, [[2:17|in all things|per omnia]], that is, in all the natural properties and in the defects that cannot be taken away [that is, the defects that belong to human nature as such, as mortality, hunger and weariness], [[2:17|to be made like|similari]] [[2:17|unto his brethren|fratribus]], that is, to other men; but not in the defects that can be taken away, namely in sin and in the lack of what is necessary. For it was not fitting that he should be lame, blind or sickly, though at the time of his passion he grew faint. He was like others, then, in that he was mortal, was suckled at the breast, grew, hungered, ate, and suffered death. [[2:17|that he might become a merciful|Ut misericors fieret]], that is, that he might bestow mercy; or, that he might become merciful in act and habit in human nature, he who is eternally merciful in the divine nature; [[2:17|and faithful high priest|et fidelis pontifex]], that is, a true mediator and priest for us, [[2:17|before God|ad Deum]] the Father, or the Trinity, by offering himself to God on the cross as a spotless victim [[Eph 5:2|for an odour of sweetness|in odorem suavitatis]]; [[2:17|that he might be a propitiation for|ut repropitiaret]], that is, that by appeasing God he might blot out, [[2:17|the sins of the people|delicta populi]], that is, of the whole human race: as John says: [[1 John 2:2|he is the propitiation for our sins|Ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris]]. Of this high priest Peter also says: [[1 Pet 2:25|you are now converted to the shepherd and bishop of your souls|Conversi estis ad pastorem et episcopum animarum vestrarum]].

paras.t: In eo enim in quo, id est in natura humana assumpta, in qua passus est ipse Christus a præside et ejus ministris, et tentatus a dæmone in deserto, atque Judæis quibus loquitur: Quid me tentatis, hypocritæ? potens est et eis qui tentantur, auxiliari ne superentur. Sua enim passione et tentatione promeruit nobis gratiam omnibus tentationibus efficaciter reluctandi; et non solum ut Deus, sed etiam ut homo, de plenitudine sua influit nobis, quemadmodum caput membris.
paras.en: [[2:18|For in that wherein|In eo enim in quo]], that is, in the human nature he assumed, in which Christ [[2:18|himself hath suffered|passus est ipse]] at the hands of the governor and his ministers, [[2:18|and been tempted|et tentatus]] by the devil in the desert, and by the Jews, to whom he says: [[Matt 22:18|Why do you tempt me, ye hypocrites?|Quid me tentatis, hypocritæ?]] [[2:18|he is able to succour them also that are tempted|potens est et eis qui tentantur, auxiliari]], lest they be overcome. For by his passion and temptation he merited for us the grace to resist all temptations effectually; and not only as God but also as man he pours into us of his fullness, as the head into the members.

3.title: ELUCIDATIO CAPITULI TERTII : UNDE, FRATRES SANCTI, VOCATIONIS CŒLESTIS PARTICIPES.
3.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly vocation.

paras.t: Ostensa excellentia Christi per comparationem ejus ad angelos et Prophetas generaliter, nunc idem ostenditur specialiter per comparationem ad Moysen: per quod etiam declaratur eminentia novi Testamenti præ veteri.
paras.en: Having shown the excellence of Christ by comparing him with the angels and with the Prophets in general, the Apostle now shows the same in particular by comparing him with Moses: by which the eminence of the New Testament over the Old is also made plain.

paras.t: Unde, fratres sancti, id est, quia sic potens est Christus auxiliari tentatis, idcirco, o fratres, sancti per regenerationem Baptismatis et munditiam religiosæ conversationis, vocationis cœlestis participes, id est, prædicationis et inspirationis ad cœlestem beatitudinem invitantis, seu gratiæ ad illam perducentis, consortes: hæc enim vobis exhibita sunt; considerate causa imitationis, apostolum, id est nuntium divinitus missum, et pontificem, id est, qui viam seu pontem veniendi ad Deum nobis ostendit ac fecit, dando exemplum, confessionis nostræ, id est pontificem quem confitemur esse verum Filium Dei salvatoremque mundi.
paras.en: [[3:1|Wherefore, holy brethren|Unde, fratres sancti]], that is, since Christ is thus able to help those who are tempted, therefore, O brethren, holy through the regeneration of Baptism and the cleanness of a religious life, [[3:1|partakers of the heavenly vocation|vocationis cœlestis participes]], that is, sharers in the preaching and inspiration that invite you to heavenly beatitude, or in the grace that leads you to it: for these have been shown to you; [[3:1|consider|considerate]], for the sake of imitation, [[3:1|the apostle|apostolum]], that is, the messenger sent by God, [[3:1|and high priest|et pontificem]], that is, him who showed and made for us the way or bridge of coming to God, by giving us an example [Denis takes *pontifex*, “high priest”, from *pons*, “bridge”], [[3:1|of our confession|confessionis nostræ]], that is, the high priest whom we confess to be the true Son of God and Saviour of the world.

paras.t: Jesus, qui fidelis est, secundum naturam assumptam, ei qui fecit illum, id est Deo Patri a quo secundum humanitatem creatus est. Dicitur autem Christus fidelis, non a fide quæ est virtus theologica, quam ipse non habuit, quoniam fuerat verus comprehensor, sed a fidelitate qua efficaciter adimplevit quidquid complacuit Patri. Propter quod ipse ait: Quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper; et: Non quæro gloriam meam, sed honorifico Patrem meum. Sicut et Moyses in omni domo ejus, id est in tota Synagoga seu Judæorum congregatione, quæ est domus Dei. Unde Dominus protestatur Aaroni et Mariæ: Servus meus Moyses in omni domo mea fidelissimus est.
paras.en: [[3:1|Jesus|Jesus]]: [[3:2|Who is faithful|qui fidelis est]], according to the nature he assumed, [[3:2|to him that made him|ei qui fecit illum]], that is, to God the Father, by whom he was created according to his humanity. Now Christ is called faithful not from faith, which is a theological virtue and which he himself did not have, since he was a true comprehensor [that is, one already enjoying the vision of God, as the blessed do, and so without need of faith], but from the fidelity by which he effectively fulfilled whatever pleased the Father. For which reason he himself says: [[John 8:29|I do always the things that please him|Quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper]]; and: [[John 8:50|I seek not my own glory|Non quæro gloriam meam]], [[John 8:49|but I honour my Father|sed honorifico Patrem meum]] [the margin’s verse number here cannot be read; the words are John 8:50 and 8:49]. [[3:2|as was also Moses in all his house|Sicut et Moyses in omni domo ejus]], that is, in the whole Synagogue or congregation of the Jews, which is the house of God. Whence the Lord declares to Aaron and Mary: [[Num 12:7|my servant Moses who is most faithful in all my house|Servus meus Moyses in omni domo mea fidelissimus est]].

paras.t: Insuper ostenditur Christus excellentior Moyse. Amplioris enim gloriæ, id est majoris dignitatis, iste Jesus præ Moyse, id est supra Moysen seu plus quam Moyses, dignus habitus est a Deo et fidelibus hominibus, quanto ampliorem honorem habet domus, id est de domo (ut scilicet Domus sit genitivi casus), ille qui fabricavit illam, id est fabricator domus, quam ejus inhabitator seu dispensator. Quod intelligendum est de principali fabricatore, qui alios ad fabricandum inducit, et ministeriali inhabitatore.
paras.en: Moreover, Christ is shown to be more excellent than Moses. [[3:3|For this man|iste Jesus]] [Denis reads *iste Jesus*, “this Jesus”] [[3:3|was counted worthy|dignus habitus est]] by God and by faithful men [[3:3|of greater glory|Amplioris enim gloriæ]], that is, of greater dignity, [[3:3|than Moses|præ Moyse]], that is, above Moses, or more than Moses, [[3:3|by so much as|quanto]] [[3:3|he that hath built the house|qui fabricavit illam]], that is, the builder of the house, [[3:3|hath greater honour than the house|ampliorem honorem habet domus]], that is, honour in respect of the house (taking *domus* as the genitive case), than its inhabitant or steward [Denis reads “greater honour of the house”, that is, over it, where the Douay-Rheims has “than the house”]. This is to be understood of the principal builder, who leads others to build, and of an inhabitant who serves in it.

paras.t: Omnis namque domus, tam materialis ex lignis atque lapidibus constans, quam spiritualis ex diversis fidelibus congregata, fabricatur ab aliquo artifice, diversas partes ad invicem copulante. Per se enim non fit; sed sicut partes materialis domus copulantur cæmento et clavis, sic personæ fideles uniuntur per fidem et caritatem. Qui autem omnia creavit, Deus est: ergo et ipse domum Ecclesiæ fabricavit. Christus autem est Deus: ergo et ipse ædificavit Ecclesiam, cujus membrum est Moyses. Christus vero est Dominus ejus: ideo habet ampliorem honorem quam Moyses.
paras.en: [[3:4|For every house|Omnis namque domus]], the material house made of wood and stones as well as the spiritual house gathered from various faithful, [[3:4|is built by some man|fabricatur ab aliquo]], some craftsman who joins its various parts to one another. For it does not come to be of itself; but as the parts of a material house are joined with mortar and nails, so faithful persons are united by faith and charity. [[3:4|but he that created all things|Qui autem omnia creavit]][[Wis 1:14||]] [[3:4|is God|Deus est]]: therefore he also built the house of the Church. Now Christ is God: therefore he too built the Church, of which Moses is a member. And Christ is its Lord: therefore he has greater honour than Moses.

paras.t: Et Moyses quidem fidelis erat in tota domo ejus, id est in omni Synagoga Judæorum, quæ fuit domus Dei, tanquam famulus, in testimonium eorum, id est ad proferendum cum attestatione divina, ea quæ dicenda erant, id est, quæ Deus jussit per eum dici ad populum.
paras.en: [[3:5|And Moses indeed was faithful in all his house|Et Moyses quidem fidelis erat in tota domo ejus]], that is, in all the Synagogue of the Jews, which was the house of God, [[3:5|as a servant|tanquam famulus]], [[3:5|for a testimony of those things|in testimonium eorum]], that is, to set forth with divine attestation those things [[3:5|which were to be said|quæ dicenda erant]], that is, which God commanded to be spoken through him to the people.

paras.t: Christus vero tanquam Filius Dei naturalis et unicus, fidelis est in domo sua, id est in Ecclesia; quæ domus sumus nos Christiani per caritatem et fidem uniti: Templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos; si fiduciam, id est actualem confidentiam, scilicet exspectationem felicitatis futuræ, et adjutorii gratiæ ad felicitatem obtinendam necessarii, et gloriam spei, id est jucunditatem cœlestem, ad quam spes tendit, usque in finem vitæ præsentis inclusive, firmam retineamus, stabiliter ac perseveranter sperando, atque futuram beatitudinem desiderando. Hoc dicit Apostolus, quia sicut ad domum materialem requiritur stabile fundamentum, ita ad domum spiritualem, scilicet, ut fideles sint domus Dei, exigitur firmitas spei ac fidei: aliter Deus non habitaret in eis per gratiam consummatam.
paras.en: [[3:6|But Christ, as the Son|Christus vero tanquam Filius]] of God, his natural and only Son, is faithful [[3:6|in his own house|in domo sua]], that is, in the Church; [[3:6|which house are we|quæ domus sumus nos]] Christians, united by charity and faith: [[1 Cor 3:17|For the temple of God is holy, which you are|Templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos]] [the margin here reads “10, 11” and “17”; the words are 1 Cor 3:17]; [[3:6|if we hold fast the confidence|si fiduciam]], that is, actual confidence, namely the expectation of future happiness, and of the help of grace needed to obtain that happiness, [[3:6|and glory of hope|et gloriam spei]], that is, the heavenly joy to which hope tends, [[3:6|unto the end|usque in finem]] of the present life inclusively, [[3:6|hold fast|firmam retineamus]], hoping steadfastly and perseveringly, and longing for the beatitude to come. The Apostle says this because, as a material house requires a firm foundation, so the spiritual house, that is, for the faithful to be the house of God, requires firmness of hope and of faith: otherwise God would not dwell in them by consummate grace.

paras.t: Ex prædictis de excellentia Christi, admonet consequenter Apostolus diligenter obedire sermoni Christi. Quapropter, id est, quum tanta sit eminentia Christi præ Moyse, sicut dicit Spiritus Sanctus in Psalmo, quod subditur: Hodie, id est tempore evangelicæ prædicationis et gratiæ, si vocem ejus, id est verba Christi, audieritis vel ab ore ejus vel ab ejus ministris, hoc est, quia ea audietis, nolite obdurare, id est verbis Dei claudere, corda vestra, ne sitis rebelles atque increduli. Hæc ad litteram dicuntur ad Judæos qui tempore Christi et postea fuerunt. Sicut in exacerbatione, id est, quemadmodum contigit, et a patribus vestris factum est in provocatione seu Dei offensione, secundum diem tentationis in deserto, quando ex infidelitate voluistis experiri potentiam meam: sicut ait Psalmista: Et tentaverunt Deum in cordibus suis, ut peterent escas animabus suis.
paras.en: From what has been said of the excellence of Christ, the Apostle next admonishes them to obey the word of Christ diligently. [[3:7|Wherefore|Quapropter]], that is, since the eminence of Christ over Moses is so great, [[3:7|as the Holy Ghost saith|sicut dicit Spiritus Sanctus]] in the Psalm[[Ps 94:8||]] [the margin gives Ps. xciv, 8, and a little lower “11”: the passage quoted in vv. 7–11 is Ps 94:8–11], in what follows: [[3:7|To-day|Hodie]], that is, in the time of the Gospel preaching and of grace, [[3:7|if you shall hear|audieritis]] [[3:7|his voice|si vocem ejus]], that is, the words of Christ, either from his own mouth or from his ministers, that is, since you will hear them, [[3:8|Harden not|nolite obdurare]], that is, close them to the words of God, [[3:8|your hearts|corda vestra]], lest you be rebellious and unbelieving. These things are said literally to the Jews who lived in the time of Christ and afterwards. [[3:8|as in the provocation|Sicut in exacerbatione]], that is, as it happened, and as was done by your fathers, in the provocation or offending of God, [[3:8|in the day of temptation in the desert|secundum diem tentationis in deserto]], when out of unbelief you wished to put my power to the test: as the Psalmist says: [[Ps 77:18|And they tempted God in their hearts, by asking meat for their desires.|Et tentaverunt Deum in cordibus suis, ut peterent escas animabus suis.]] [the margin gives Ps. xciv, 9, the verse of the Psalm quoted here; the words Denis gives are Ps 77:18].

paras.t: Ubi, id est in quo deserto, […] frequenter. Unde Dominus ait ad Moysen in Numeris: Tentaverunt me jam per decem vices. Probaverunt, id est, experti sunt quid agere possem, et viderunt opera mea mirabilia in Ægypto, in mari Rubro, in deserto, quadraginta annis. Tanto enim tempore in deserto fuerunt vel circiter.
paras.en: [[3:9|Where|Ubi]], that is, in which desert, […] frequently. Whence the Lord says to Moses in Numbers: They [[Num 14:22|have tempted me now ten times|Tentaverunt me jam per decem vices]]. [[3:9|proved|Probaverunt]], that is, they found out what I could do, [[3:9|and saw my works|et viderunt opera mea]], my wonderful works, in Egypt, in the Red Sea, in the desert, [[3:10|Forty years|quadraginta annis]]. For they were in the desert that long, or about that long[[Deut 8:2||]].

paras.t: Propter quod, id est ob tantam perversitatem istorum, offensus, id est iratus, fui generationi huic, id est hominibus istis incredulis, et dixi per angelum seu Moysen: Semper hi errant corde, id est, intellectum excæcatum habent, et ex malitia peccant. Ipsi vero non cognoverunt, id est, spiritualiter non intellexerunt, vias meas, id est opera mea miraculosa ac justa: quæ viæ vocantur, quia perducunt ad Dei notitiam. Unde in Deuteronomio Moyses loquitur: Vos, inquit, vidistis universa magnalia quæ coram nobis Dominus fecit, et non dedit vobis Dominus cor intelligens, et oculos videntes usque in præsentem diem.
paras.en: [[3:10|for which cause|Propter quod]], that is, because of so great a perversity of theirs, [[3:10|I was offended|offensus]], that is, angered, [[3:10|with this generation|fui generationi huic]], that is, with these unbelieving men, [[3:10|and I said|et dixi]] through an angel or through Moses: [[3:10|They always err in heart|Semper hi errant corde]], that is, they have a blinded understanding, and sin out of malice. [[3:10|And they have not known|Ipsi vero non cognoverunt]], that is, they have not understood spiritually, [[3:10|my ways|vias meas]], that is, my miraculous and just works: which are called ways because they lead to the knowledge of God. Whence Moses speaks in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 29:2|You|Vos]], he says, [[Deut 29:2|have seen all the things that the Lord did before you|vidistis universa magnalia quæ coram nobis Dominus fecit]] [Denis has *magnalia*, “great works”, and “before us”], [[Deut 29:4|And the Lord hath not given you a heart to understand, and eyes to see|et non dedit vobis Dominus cor intelligens, et oculos videntes]] [[Deut 29:4|unto this present day|usque in præsentem diem]].

paras.t: Quibus juravi, id est, firmiter dixi per Moysen, in ira mea, id est in zelo justitiæ meæ, quo eorum peccata vindicare proposui: Si introibunt, id est, non intrabunt, in requiem meam, id est terram promissionis, in qua eis, si non peccassent, mansionem quietam dedissem. Hoc Deus juravit, quando filii Israel murmuraverunt contra Dominum, auditis sermonibus nuntiorum qui exploraverunt terram Chanaan. Tunc enim juravit, quod nemo eorum qui murmuraverunt, ingrederetur hanc terram præter Caleb et Josue.
paras.en: [[3:11|As I have sworn|Quibus juravi]] [Denis reads *quibus juravi*, “to whom I swore”], that is, said firmly through Moses, [[3:11|in my wrath|in ira mea]], that is, in the zeal of my justice, by which I resolved to punish their sins: [[3:11|If they shall enter|Si introibunt]], that is, they shall not enter [a Hebrew form of oath, in which “if they shall enter” means “they shall not enter”], [[3:11|into my rest|in requiem meam]], that is, the land of promise, in which I would have given them a quiet dwelling had they not sinned[[Ex 23:22||]] [the margin gives Exod. xxiii, 22 and following]. God swore this when the children of Israel murmured against the Lord, having heard the reports of the messengers who had explored the land of Chanaan[[Num 14:1||]]. For then he swore that none of those who had murmured would enter this land except Caleb and Josue [the margin gives only Num. xiv; the oath is at Num 14:28–30].

paras.t: Ex præallegata Scriptura infert Apostolus salutarem doctrinam. Videte, fratres, ne forte sit in aliquo vestrum cor malum incredulitatis, id est mens vitiosa perfidiæ subdita, discedendi, id est paratum discedere seu averti, a Deo vivo: a quo disceditur per inobedientiam, non per localem distantiam, juxta illud Osee: Dereliquerunt Dominum in non custodiendo.
paras.en: From the Scripture alleged above, the Apostle draws a wholesome teaching. [[3:12|Take heed, brethren, lest perhaps there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief|Videte, fratres, ne forte sit in aliquo vestrum cor malum incredulitatis]], that is, a vicious mind subject to faithlessness, [[3:12|to depart|discedendi]], that is, ready to depart or turn away, [[3:12|from the living God|a Deo vivo]]: from whom one departs by disobedience, not by distance of place, according to that word of Osee: [[Osee 4:10|they have forsaken the Lord in not observing the law|Dereliquerunt Dominum in non custodiendo]] [the margin gives Osee ix, 10; the words are Osee 4:10].

paras.t: Sed adhortamini vosmetipsos per singulos dies, id est, quotidie admonete vos invicem, seu quilibet semetipsum verbis sacræ Scripturæ, donec Hodie cognominatur, id est, quamdiu tempus gratiæ durat et esse asseritur: de quo alibi dicitur, Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis. De hoc scriptum est per Zachariam: Applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum in die illo. Ut non obduretur quis ex vobis, id est, ne aliquis vestrum obstinatus fiat, seu habituatus in malo, fallacia peccati, id est delectatione alliciente et rationem excæcante, quæ est in peccato. Peccatum namque delectat: unde et tristitiam promeretur.
paras.en: [[3:13|But exhort one another every day|Sed adhortamini vosmetipsos per singulos dies]], that is, admonish one another daily, or each one himself, with the words of sacred Scripture [the margin here reads “Ibid. 28–35”, which fits nothing in this passage; it may belong with Num 14:28–35, the oath recounted under v. 11], [[3:13|whilst it is called to day|donec Hodie cognominatur]], that is, as long as the time of grace lasts and is declared to be: of which it is said elsewhere, [[2 Cor 6:2|Behold, now is the acceptable time: behold, now is the day of salvation|Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis]]. Of this day it is written through Zacharias: [[Zach 2:11|many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day|Applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum in die illo]]. [[3:13|that none of you be hardened|Ut non obduretur quis ex vobis]], that is, lest any of you become obstinate, or habituated in evil, [[3:13|through the deceitfulness of sin|fallacia peccati]], that is, through the delight which is in sin, enticing and blinding the reason. For sin delights: and for that reason it also deserves sorrow.

paras.t: Participes enim Christi effecti sumus, id est, Christo incorporati sumus ut membra capiti, et de plenitudine ejus accepimus, ejus quoque hereditatis consortes erimus; si tamen initium substantiæ ejus, id est, si fidem formatam, per quam primum Deo conjungimur et ejus possessio efficimur, usque ad finem, id est perseveranter, firmum retineamus, id est, stabiles et efficaces in fide manserimus; dum dicitur, id est, quamdiu dicitur nobis: Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis, nolite obdurare corda vestra, quemadmodum in illa exacerbatione.
paras.en: [[3:14|For we are made partakers of Christ|Participes enim Christi effecti sumus]], that is, we have been incorporated into Christ as members into the head, and of his fullness we have received, and we shall also be sharers in his inheritance; [[3:14|yet so, if we hold the beginning of his substance|si tamen initium substantiæ ejus]], that is, formed faith [that is, faith given life by charity], by which we are first joined to God and become his possession, [[3:14|unto the end|usque ad finem]], that is, perseveringly, [[3:14|firm|firmum retineamus]], that is, if we remain steadfast and effectual in faith; [[3:15|While it is said|dum dicitur]], that is, as long as it is said to us: [[3:15|To day, if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in that provocation|Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis, nolite obdurare corda vestra, quemadmodum in illa exacerbatione]].

paras.t: Quidam enim Judæorum in deserto audientes verba Dei, exacerbaverunt, id est, non credendo et impie operando, Deum graviter offenderunt seu provocaverunt. Non quod invariabilis Deus veraciter irritetur vel exacerbetur, de quo legitur, Tu autem, dominator Domine, cum tranquillitate judicas, et cum magna reverentia disponis nos; sed quia per modum exacerbati se habet, dum nostra peccata districte ulciscitur. Ideo apud Jeremiam dicitur: Numquid me ad iracundiam provocant? dicit Dominus. Nonne semetipsos in confusione vultus sui? Sed non universi qui profecti sunt ab Ægypto per Moysen, id est, non omnes Deum exacerbaverunt, qui per Moysis ducatum exierunt Ægyptum. Caleb enim et Josue non offenderunt tam graviter.
paras.en: [[3:16|For some|Quidam enim]] of the Jews in the desert, [[3:16|who heard|audientes]] the words of God, [[3:16|did provoke|exacerbaverunt]], that is, by not believing and by acting wickedly, they gravely offended or provoked God. Not that the unchangeable God is truly irritated or provoked, he of whom we read: [[Wis 12:18|But thou being master of power, judgest with tranquillity, and with great favour disposest of us|Tu autem, dominator Domine, cum tranquillitate judicas, et cum magna reverentia disponis nos]] [Denis has *dominator Domine*, “O Lord, the ruler”, where the Vulgate has *dominator virtutis*, “master of power”]; but because he acts in the manner of one provoked, when he strictly punishes our sins. Therefore it is said in Jeremias: [[Jer 7:19|Do they provoke me to anger, saith the Lord? is it not themselves, to the confusion of their own countenance?|Numquid me ad iracundiam provocant? dicit Dominus. Nonne semetipsos in confusione vultus sui?]] [[3:16|but not all that came out of Egypt by Moses|Sed non universi qui profecti sunt ab Ægypto per Moysen]], that is, not all who went out of Egypt under the leadership of Moses provoked God. For Caleb and Josue did not offend so gravely.

paras.t: Quibus autem offensus, id est iratus, est Deus in deserto quadraginta annis, quibus filii Israel in deserto ambulaverunt (non quod quotidie peccaverunt ita enormiter, sed quia frequenter sic peccaverunt)? Nonne illis qui peccaverunt enormiter, discredendo, Deum tentando seu murmurando, quorum cadavera prostrata, id est dejecta et bestiis tradita, sunt in deserto?
paras.en: [[3:17|And with whom was he offended|Quibus autem offensus]], that is, angered (God, that is, in the desert), [[3:17|forty years|quadraginta annis]], the years in which the children of Israel walked in the desert (not that they sinned so enormously every day, but because they often sinned so)? [[3:17|Was it not with them that sinned|Nonne illis qui peccaverunt]] enormously, by disbelieving, by tempting God or by murmuring, [[3:17|whose carcasses were overthrown|quorum cadavera prostrata]], that is, cast down and given over to the beasts, [[3:17|in the desert|sunt in deserto]]?

paras.t: Quibus autem juravit non introire in requiem ipsius, id est in terram promissionis, nisi illis qui increduli fuerunt verbis Caleb et Josue? Qui cum aliis nuntiis redeuntes, dixerunt: Nolite rebelles esse contra Dominum, neque timeatis populum terræ hujus, quia sicut panem, ita possumus eos devorare; Dominus nobiscum est, nolite timere. Quid autem fecerunt increduli? Voluerunt utique lapidibus opprimere eos. Et videmus oculo fidei, testimonio Scripturarum, quia non potuerunt introire in requiem ipsius, id est in terram hanc, Deo eos prohibente, propter incredulitatem ipsorum.
paras.en: [[3:18|And to whom did he swear, that they should not enter into his rest|Quibus autem juravit non introire in requiem ipsius]], that is, into the land of promise, [[3:18|but to them that were incredulous|nisi illis qui increduli fuerunt]] to the words of Caleb and Josue? For these, returning with the other messengers, said: [[Num 14:9|Be not rebellious against the Lord: and fear ye not the people of this land, for we are able to eat them up as bread|Nolite rebelles esse contra Dominum, neque timeatis populum terræ hujus, quia sicut panem, ita possumus eos devorare]]; [[Num 14:9|the Lord is with us, fear ye not|Dominus nobiscum est, nolite timere]] [the margin’s verse number here is lost; the words are Num 14:9]. And what did the unbelievers do? Indeed they [[Num 14:10|would have stoned them|lapidibus opprimere eos]]. [[3:19|And we see|Et videmus]] with the eye of faith, by the testimony of the Scriptures, [[3:19|that they could not enter in|quia non potuerunt introire]] into his rest, that is, into this land, God forbidding them, [[3:19|because of unbelief|propter incredulitatem]], their own unbelief.

4.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI QUARTI : TIMEAMUS ERGO, NE FORTE RELICTA POLLICITATIONE, ETC.
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: Let us fear therefore lest the promise being left, etc.

paras.t: Denique, ex præinducta auctoritate Sacræ Scripturæ hortatur Apostolus ad debitam sollicitudinem. Timeamus ergo, id est, quoniam illi Judæi propter suam incredulitatem et murmurationem prohibiti sunt introire terram promissionis, idcirco formidemus, ne forte relicta pollicitatione, id est oblita seu spreta promissione divina nobis facta, introeundi, id est de ingressu nostro post hanc vitam, in requiem ejus cœlestem, id est felicitatem æternam, existimetur aliquis ex nobis deesse, id est, aliquis nostrum inveniatur a consecutione hujus promissæ quietis deficere propter negligentiam suam. Nam inexcusabiles sumus, si eam non obtinemus. Cujus ratio subinfertur: Etenim et nobis annuntiatum est, id est a Christo in Evangelio prædicatum de requie cœlesti, quemadmodum et illis Judæis per Moysen annuntiatum est de requie terrena. Ait enim Salvator: Beati pauperes spiritu, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cœlorum; et alibi, In futura resurrectione nec nubent neque nubentur, sed erunt sicut angeli Dei; et rursus, Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi sum ego, et illi sunt mecum, ut videant claritatem meam.
paras.en: Lastly, from the authority of Holy Scripture brought forward above, the Apostle exhorts to due solicitude. [[4:1|Let us fear therefore|Timeamus ergo]]: that is, since those Jews were barred from entering the land of promise for their unbelief and murmuring, let us therefore be afraid [[4:1|lest|ne forte]], [[4:1|the promise being left|relicta pollicitatione]], that is, the divine promise made to us being forgotten or despised, [[4:1|of entering|introeundi]], that is, of our entrance after this life, [[4:1|into his rest|in requiem ejus]], his heavenly rest, that is, eternal happiness, [[4:1|any of you should be thought to be wanting|existimetur aliquis ex nobis deesse]] [Denis reads “ex nobis”, “of us”, where the Vulgate has “ex vobis”, “of you”], that is, any of us should be found to fall short of attaining this promised rest through his own negligence. For we are without excuse if we do not obtain it. The reason for this is added: [[4:2|For unto us also it hath been declared|Etenim et nobis annuntiatum est]], that is, it was preached by Christ in the Gospel concerning the heavenly rest, [[4:2|in like manner as unto them|quemadmodum et illis]], the Jews, to whom it was declared through Moses concerning an earthly rest. For the Saviour says: [[Matt 5:3|Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven|Beati pauperes spiritu, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cœlorum]]; and elsewhere: [[Matt 22:30|in the resurrection they shall neither marry nor be married, but shall be as the angels of God|In futura resurrectione nec nubent neque nubentur, sed erunt sicut angeli Dei]]; and again: [[John 17:24|Father, I will that where I am, they also whom thou hast given me may be with me: that they may see my glory|Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi sum ego, et illi sunt mecum, ut videant claritatem meam]].

paras.t: Sed non profuit illis Judæis sermo auditus, id est, quem a Moyse audierunt de possessione terræ promissæ, non admixtus fidei, id est non receptus fideliter: fidei, inquam, habendæ ex his, id est de his, quæ audierunt, id est de bonis sibi promissis. Et hoc patet ex opposito:
paras.en: [[4:2|But the word of hearing did not profit them|Sed non profuit illis Judæis sermo auditus]], the Jews: that is, the word which they heard from Moses about possessing the promised land, [[4:2|not being mixed with faith|non admixtus fidei]], that is, not received faithfully: with faith, I say, to be had [[4:2|of those things|ex his]], that is, concerning those things, [[4:2|they heard|quæ audierunt]], that is, concerning the good things promised to them. And this is plain from the opposite:

paras.t: Ingrediemur enim in requiem sempiternam, qui credidimus verbis auditis de promissione illius quietis fide formata, de qua ait Christus: Omnis qui vivit et credit in me, non morietur in æternum: quemadmodum dixit, id est, sicut Spiritus Sanctus ex opposito de incredulis protestatus est, in psalmo præallegato dicens: Sicut juravi in ira mea, Si introibunt, id est, non intrabunt, in requiem meam, id est terram promissionis: sicut in præcedenti articulo explanatum est plenius.
paras.en: For we [[4:3|shall enter into rest|Ingrediemur enim in requiem]] everlasting, [[4:3|who have believed|qui credidimus]], with formed faith [that is, faith given its form by charity], the words we heard about the promise of that rest; of which Christ says: [[John 11:26|every one that liveth and believeth in me shall not die for ever|Omnis qui vivit et credit in me, non morietur in æternum]] [the margin gives only John xi; the words are John 11:26]: [[4:3|as he said|quemadmodum dixit]], that is, as the Holy Ghost, conversely, declared of the unbelievers, saying in the psalm cited above: [[4:3|As I have sworn in my wrath|Sicut juravi in ira mea]], [[4:3|If they shall enter|Si introibunt]], that is, they shall not enter, [[4:3|into my rest|in requiem meam]][[Ps 94:11||]], that is, the land of promise: as was explained more fully in the preceding article[[Heb 3:11||]].

paras.t: Et quidem operibus ab institutione mundi perfectis. Jam in superioribus mentionem fecit Apostolus de temporali requie Judæis promissa, atque ex hoc intulit de promissione æternæ quietis nobis in cœlis promissæ. In quibus verbis supponitur, quod temporalis illa requies fuit figura requiei cœlestis. Et hoc nunc probat Apostolus; simulque ostendit, quando annuntiatum est de requie sempiterna.
paras.en: [[4:3|and this indeed when the works from the foundation of the world were finished|Et quidem operibus ab institutione mundi perfectis]]. Above, the Apostle made mention of the temporal rest promised to the Jews, and from this he inferred the promise of the eternal rest promised to us in heaven. In these words it is assumed that that temporal rest was a figure of the heavenly rest. And this the Apostle now proves, and at the same time shows when the everlasting rest was announced.

paras.t: Et quidem: tanquam dicat, Nuntiatum est nobis de requie illa: quod utique factum est, operibus, id est creaturis, ab institutione mundi, id est, quæ a principio creationis fieri cœperunt, perfectis, id est distinctis atque ornatis usque ad sextum diem, in quo creatus est homo. In illis namque sex diebus perfectæ sunt species rerum. Post consummationem itaque operum sex dierum, statim facta est mentio in Scripturis de requie quadam, non temporali, sed sempiterna. Dixit enim Scriptura seu Spiritus Sanctus in quodam loco de die septimo, sic, sicut subjungitur (dies quippe dominica erat prima, ergo et sabbatum septima): Et requievit Deus, id est, operari cessavit, et in semetipso quievit, die septimo ab omnibus operibus suis ante productis, id est novis rerum speciebus creandis: quia ex tunc non creavit opera nova secundum speciem sive materiam. Nihilo minus de materia tunc facta, et ad similitudinem tunc factorum, nunc usque operatur, animas rationales creando, et totum universum administrando, atque per causas secundas plurima producendo. Propter quod ait Salvator: Pater meus usque modo operatur, et ego operor.
paras.en: [[4:3|and this indeed|Et quidem]]: as if he were saying, It was announced to us concerning that rest; and this was done [[4:3|when the works|operibus]], that is, the creatures, [[4:3|from the foundation of the world|ab institutione mundi]], that is, those which began to be made from the beginning of creation, [[4:3|were finished|perfectis]], that is, distinguished and adorned up to the sixth day, on which man was created[[Gen 1:27||]]. For in those six days the species of things were completed[[Gen 1:31||]]. So after the completion of the works of the six days, mention was at once made in the Scriptures of a certain rest[[Gen 2:2||]], not temporal but everlasting. [[4:4|For in a certain place he spoke|Dixit enim]] (that is, Scripture, or the Holy Ghost) [[4:4|of the seventh day|in quodam loco de die septimo]], that is, the sabbath, [[4:4|thus|sic]], as follows (for the Lord's day was the first, and so the sabbath the seventh): [[4:4|And God rested|Et requievit Deus]], that is, ceased from working and rested in himself, [[4:4|the seventh day from all his works|die septimo ab omnibus operibus suis]][[Gen 2:2||]] brought forth before, that is, from creating new species of things: for from then on he did not create new works as to species or matter. Nevertheless, out of the matter then made, and after the likeness of the things then made, he works until now, by creating rational souls, by governing the whole universe, and by producing very many things through secondary causes. Wherefore the Saviour says: [[John 5:17|My Father worketh until now; and I work|Pater meus usque modo operatur, et ego operor]].

paras.t: Virtus ergo rationis et intellectus hujus scripturæ consistit in hoc: Quum ab exordio describitur productio mundi, fit mentio de quadam requie qua Deus quievit. Hæc autem requies est cœlestis, non temporalis, sed per temporalem designatur. Requies enim Dei in se ipso communicatur electis in patria, ut et ipsi in Deo immediate quiescant, qui in nullo possunt alio contenti reddi seu quieti. Non enim sufficit rationali creaturæ nisi bonum immensum. Ergo de requie nobis in cœlis parata, fit mentio ante legem, in qua et figurata est requies vera, cœlestis et sempiterna.
paras.en: So the force of the reasoning and of the sense of this scripture lies in this: when the making of the world is described from its beginning, mention is made of a certain rest with which God rested. Now this rest is heavenly, not temporal, but it is signified by a temporal one. For the rest of God in himself is communicated to the elect in the fatherland [that is, in heaven], so that they too may rest in God immediately, since they can be made content or at rest in nothing else; for nothing suffices a rational creature but an immeasurable good. So mention is made, before the law, of the rest prepared for us in heaven; and in the law too the true rest, heavenly and everlasting, was prefigured.

paras.t: Consequenter ostenditur, quod etiam post legislationem fit sermo de requie sempiterna sub figura temporalis quietis. Et in isto rursum, id est, in psalmo jam dicto, iterum dicit Spiritus Sanctus: Si introibunt in requiem meam, id est, increduli illi tempore Moysis exsistentes, non ingredientur terram promissionis. Per quod designatur, quod impii cœlestem requiem non intrabunt.
paras.en: Next it is shown that after the giving of the law, too, there is talk of the everlasting rest under the figure of a temporal rest. [[4:5|And in this place again|Et in isto rursum]], that is, in the psalm already mentioned, the Holy Ghost says once more: [[4:5|If they shall enter into my rest|Si introibunt in requiem meam]], that is, those unbelievers living in the time of Moses shall not enter the land of promise. By which it is signified that the wicked shall not enter the heavenly rest.

paras.t: Quoniam ergo superest, id est restat, quosdam electos introire in illam requiem beatam ac figuratam, et hi quibus prioribus, id est Judæis quibus ante nos annuntiatum est per Moysen de ingressu terræ promissionis seu requiei temporalis, non introierunt eam propter incredulitatem suam; iterum terminat, id est Scriptura sacra determinat seu inducit, diem quemdam Hodie, id est tempus gratiæ, quod vocatum est Hodie, quoniam quotidianum est, et durat usque in finem sæculi. De quo die dictum est Romanis: Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit; et in Isaia, In illa die erit germen Domini (id est Christus Filius Dei, de quo alibi legitur: Suscitabo David germen justum) in magnificentia et gloria. In David, id est in psalmo a David composito, dicendo post tantum temporis, id est post tam longum spatium, ex quo illa dicta sunt patribus in deserto per Moysen: David enim propheta longo tempore post Moysen fuit; sicut supra dictum est de die isto capitulo præcedenti, jamque repetitur: Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis, nolite obdurare corda vestra: quæ verba satis jam declarata sunt.
paras.en: [[4:6|Seeing then it remaineth|Quoniam ergo superest]], that is, it is left, [[4:6|that some|quosdam]] of the elect [[4:6|are to enter into it|introire in illam]], into that blessed and prefigured rest, [[4:6|and they to whom it was first|et hi quibus prioribus]] (that is, the Jews, to whom, before us, it was) [[4:6|preached|annuntiatum est]] through Moses concerning the entry into the land of promise, or the temporal rest, [[4:6|did not enter|non introierunt eam]] [[4:6|because of unbelief|propter incredulitatem suam]]: [[4:7|Again he limiteth|iterum terminat]], that is, Holy Scripture determines or brings in, [[4:7|a certain day|diem quemdam]], [[4:7|To day|Hodie]], that is, the time of grace, which is called To-day because it is daily, and lasts until the end of the world. Of this day it was said to the Romans: [[Rom 13:12|The night is passed And the day is at hand|Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit]]; and in Isaias: [[Is 4:2|In that day the bud of the Lord|In illa die erit germen Domini]] (that is, Christ the Son of God, of whom we read elsewhere: [[Jer 23:5|I will raise up to David a just branch|Suscitabo David germen justum]] [“germen” is the same word that is “bud” in Isaias and “branch” in Jeremias]) [[Is 4:2|shall be in magnificence and glory|in magnificentia et gloria]]. [[4:7|in David|In David]], that is, in the psalm composed by David, [[4:7|saying|dicendo]], [[4:7|after so long a time|post tantum temporis]], that is, after so long a space since those things were said to the fathers in the desert through Moses: for David the prophet lived a long time after Moses; [[4:7|as it is above said|sicut supra dictum est]] of this day in the preceding chapter, and is now repeated: [[4:7|To day if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts|Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis, nolite obdurare corda vestra]]: words which have already been explained enough.

paras.t: Ex his palam est, quod David loquatur de alia terra et requie, quam illa quam Moyses promisit, et ad quam Josue introduxit. Illa enim ante tempora David possessa fuit a filiis Israel. Dum ergo David admonet eos qui terram promissionis possederunt, ut quum audierint vocem Dei, non obdurent corda sua, significat eos ad aliam requiem, scilicet cœlestem patriam, ingressuros, si obedierint Deo. Quod figuratum fuit in eis qui terram promissionis ingressi sunt. Ideo sequitur:
paras.en: From this it is plain that David is speaking of another land and another rest than that which Moses promised and into which Josue led them in. For that land was possessed by the children of Israel before the time of David. So when David admonishes those who possessed the land of promise not to harden their hearts when they hear the voice of God, he signifies that they will enter into another rest, namely the heavenly fatherland, if they obey God. This was prefigured in those who entered the land of promise. Therefore there follows:

paras.t: Nam si eis, videlicet filiis Israel, Jesus Christus, qui (ut Judas dicit) populum salvans de Ægypto, eos qui non crediderunt perdidit (quod convenit Jesu secundum suam divinam naturam, secundum quam vere æternus est), requiem veram atque finalem præstitisset in terra promissionis. Vel per Jesum intelligitur Josue, qui distinctus est Osee et Jesus, qui minister fuit donationis terræ istius. Nunquam Spiritus Sanctus per David de alia loqueretur posthac die, id est, in nullo tempore post diem seu requiem illam loqueretur de alia requie hac die, id est, quæ nobis annuntiatur atque proponitur hodie, utpote tempore gratiæ.
paras.en: [[4:8|For if|Nam si]] to them, namely the children of Israel, [[4:8|Jesus|Jesus]] Christ, who (as Jude says) [[Jude 1:5|having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, did afterwards destroy them that believed not|populum salvans de Ægypto, eos qui non crediderunt perdidit]] (which belongs to Jesus according to his divine nature, by which he is truly eternal), [[4:8|had given|præstitisset]] true and final [[4:8|rest|requiem]] in the land of promise. Or by Jesus is understood Josue, who was known by two names, Osee and Jesus [Josue was first called Osee; “Jesus” is the Greek form of his name], and who was the minister of the giving of that land. The Holy Ghost [[4:8|would never|Nunquam]], through David, [[4:8|have afterwards spoken of another day|de alia loqueretur posthac die]]: that is, at no time after that day, or that rest, would he speak of another rest, this day: that is, the one which is announced and set before us to-day, namely in the time of grace.

paras.t: Itaque relinquitur, id est, paratur et conservatur, sabbatismus, id est plena quies in cœlo, significata per sabbatum et terræ promissionis quietem, populo Dei, id est electis fidelibus, qui ad cœnam nuptiarum Agni vocati sunt.
paras.en: [[4:9|There remaineth therefore|Itaque relinquitur]], that is, there is prepared and kept, [[4:9|a day of rest|sabbatismus]] [“sabbatismus”, a sabbath-keeping], that is, full rest in heaven, signified by the sabbath and by the rest of the land of promise, [[4:9|for the people of God|populo Dei]], that is, for the faithful elect, who [[Apoc 19:9|are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb|ad cœnam nuptiarum Agni vocati sunt]].

paras.t: Qui enim ingressus est in requiem ejus, id est, qui cœlestem quietem adeptus est, etiam ipse requievit ab operibus suis, id est laboriosis exercitiis vitæ præsentis, sicut et a suis operibus Deus quievit septimo die. Unde et legimus: Beati mortui qui in Domino moriuntur; amodo jam dicit Spiritus, ut requiescant a laboribus suis. Nec obstat quod in Apocalypsi asseritur, Requiem non habebant, die ac nocte dicentia, Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus, etc., quia requies sumitur ibi improprie, pro cessatione ab actu. Sancti autem in patria indesinenter aliquid agunt, Deum laudando, amando, videndo. Proprie autem requies sumitur pro cessatione a labore aut motu.
paras.en: [[4:10|For he that is entered into his rest|Qui enim ingressus est in requiem ejus]], that is, he who has attained the heavenly rest, [[4:10|the same also hath rested from his works|etiam ipse requievit ab operibus suis]], that is, from the toilsome exercises of the present life, [[4:10|as God did from his|sicut et a suis operibus Deus]] works, resting on the seventh day. Hence too we read: [[Apoc 14:13|Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord. From henceforth now, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours|Beati mortui qui in Domino moriuntur; amodo jam dicit Spiritus, ut requiescant a laboribus suis]]. Nor does it stand in the way that the Apocalypse says, [[Apoc 4:8|they rested not day and night, saying: Holy, Holy, Holy|Requiem non habebant, die ac nocte dicentia, Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus]], etc.; for rest is taken there improperly, for ceasing from activity. And the saints in the fatherland are unceasingly doing something: praising, loving, seeing God. But properly rest is taken for ceasing from labour or from motion.

paras.t: Festinemus ergo ingredi, ferventer amando et efficaciter operando, in illam requiem sempiternam, ut ne in id ipsum quis incidat incredulitatis exemplum, id est, ne aliquis nostrum incidat in eamdem pœnam quam infideles Judæi inciderunt propter incredulitatem: quæ pœna nobis in exemplum proponitur, quatenus eam considerando, vitemus peccata, propter quæ infligitur. Cur autem testimonium sit, subditur:
paras.en: [[4:11|Let us hasten therefore to enter|Festinemus ergo ingredi]], by loving fervently and working effectually, [[4:11|into that rest|in illam requiem]] everlasting: [[4:11|lest any man fall into the same example of unbelief|ut ne in id ipsum quis incidat incredulitatis exemplum]], that is, lest any of us fall into the same punishment into which the unbelieving Jews fell for their unbelief: a punishment set before us as an example, so that, by considering it, we may avoid the sins for which it is inflicted. And why it is a testimony [that is, why this example stands as a warning to us] is added next:

paras.t: Vivus est enim sermo Dei, id est Verbum seu unigenitus Filius Dei. Sicut enim Pater habet vitam in semetipso, sic dedit et Filio vitam habere in semetipso. Et efficax, id est omnipotens, prout Sapiens ait: Dum medium silentium contineret omnia, omnipotens sermo tuus, Domine, a regalibus sedibus venit; et rursus idem, Omnium enim est artifex, omnem habens virtutem, omnia prospiciens. Et penetrabilior, id est acutior, omni gladio ancipiti, id est ex utraque parte acuto. Non enim potest gladius tam intime corpori imprimi, quam intime Filius Dei illabitur omnibus rerum essentiis. Quum namque sit verus Deus, omnia penetrat, implet et continet; estque intimior omni rei, quam ipsa aut pars ejus sibi.
paras.en: [[4:12|For the word of God is living|Vivus est enim sermo Dei]], that is, the Word or only-begotten Son of God. [[John 5:26|For as the Father hath life in himself, so he hath given to the Son also to have life in himself|Sicut enim Pater habet vitam in semetipso, sic dedit et Filio vitam habere in semetipso]]. [[4:12|and effectual|Et efficax]], that is, almighty, as the Wise Man says: [[Wis 18:14|while all things were in quiet silence|Dum medium silentium contineret omnia]], [[Wis 18:15|Thy Almighty word|omnipotens sermo tuus]], O Lord, came [[Wis 18:15|from thy royal throne|a regalibus sedibus]] [Denis reads “medium silentium”, “the midst of silence”, and “venit”, “came”, where the Vulgate has “quietum silentium” and “leaped down”]; and again the same writer: [[Wis 7:21|the worker of all things|Omnium enim est artifex]], [[Wis 7:23|having all power, overseeing all things|omnem habens virtutem, omnia prospiciens]] [Denis joins words of Wis 7:21 and 7:23]. [[4:12|and more piercing|Et penetrabilior]], that is, sharper, [[4:12|than any two edged sword|omni gladio ancipiti]], that is, sharp on either side. For a sword cannot be driven into a body as inwardly as the Son of God enters into the essences of all things. For since he is true God, he penetrates, fills and contains all things; and he is more inward to each thing than that thing, or any part of it, is to itself.

paras.t: Et pertingens usque ad divisionem animæ ac spiritus, id est tam intimus homini, ut inter sensualitatem et rationem discernat. Vel, per animam et spiritum eadem hominis forma signatur: quæ dicitur anima, quantum ad vires sensitivas; et spiritus, quantum ad vires intellectivas. Tanta est autem perspicacitas Verbi Dei, ut distinguat animam secundum partem sensitivam, a se ipsa secundum partem intellectivam. Compagum quoque et medullarum, id est, subtilissima quæque corporis interiora perspicit et distinguit. Compages autem sunt junctura corporis, nervis colligatæ; medullæ vero intra ossa inclusæ sunt. Et hic sermo, Verbum, seu Filius Dei, est discretor, id est dijudicator et cognitor, cogitationum, non solum earum quæ sunt in virtute cogitativa organica, sed et earum quæ sunt in potentia intellectiva inorganica, et intentionum cordis, id est ordinationum finalium. Deus quippe non solum inspicit cogitationes, sed cernit ad quem finem quælibet cogitatio ordinetur a cogitante. Unde Job dicit: Scio quia omnia potes, et nulla te latet cogitatio. Et iterum Scriptura: Homo videt ea quæ parent, Deus autem intuetur cor.
paras.en: [[4:12|and reaching unto the division of the soul and the spirit|Et pertingens usque ad divisionem animæ ac spiritus]], that is, so inward to man that he discerns between sensuality and reason. Or: by soul and spirit the same form of man is meant, which is called soul as regards the powers of sense, and spirit as regards the powers of the intellect. And so great is the penetration of the Word of God that he distinguishes the soul as to its sensitive part from itself as to its intellective part. [[4:12|of the joints also and the marrow|Compagum quoque et medullarum]]: that is, he sees through and distinguishes all the subtlest inward parts of the body. The joints are the junctures of the body, bound together by sinews; and the marrow is enclosed within the bones. And this word, the Word or Son of God, [[4:12|is a discerner|est discretor]], that is, a judge and knower, [[4:12|of the thoughts|cogitationum]], not only of those that are in the cogitative power, which works through a bodily organ, but also of those in the intellective power, which has no bodily organ, [[4:12|and intents of the heart|et intentionum cordis]], that is, of the ends to which they are directed. For God not only looks upon the thoughts, but sees to what end each thought is directed by the one who thinks it. Hence Job says: [[Job 42:2|I know that thou canst do all things, and no thought is hid from thee|Scio quia omnia potes, et nulla te latet cogitatio]]. And again Scripture: [[1 Kings 16:7|man seeth those things that appear, but the Lord beholdeth the heart|Homo videt ea quæ parent, Deus autem intuetur cor]] [Denis has “Deus”, “God”, where the Vulgate has “Dominus”, “the Lord”].

paras.t: Et non est ulla creatura invisibilis in conspectu ejus, id est, omnia sine exceptione manifesta seu nota sunt conspectui Filii Dei. Pater enim diligit Filium, et omnia demonstrat ei quæ ipse facit. Omnia autem nuda, id est intime certa et sine velamine patula, et aperta sunt oculis ejus, id est menti ejus divinæ: imo et animæ Christi omnia creata sunt cognita. Ideo scriptum est: Oculi Domini multo plus lucidiores super solem, circumspicientes omnes vias hominum: Domino enim Deo antequam crearentur, omnia sunt cognita. Ad quem increatum Dei sermonem seu Filium, est nobis sermo, id est, ei tanquam judici nos adstare, et rationem reddere oportebit.
paras.en: [[4:13|Neither is there any creature invisible in his sight|Et non est ulla creatura invisibilis in conspectu ejus]], that is, all things without exception are manifest or known to the sight of the Son of God. [[John 5:20|For the Father loveth the Son and sheweth him all things which himself doth|Pater enim diligit Filium, et omnia demonstrat ei quæ ipse facit]]. [[4:13|but all things are naked|Omnia autem nuda]], that is, inwardly certain and lying open without a veil, [[4:13|and open to his eyes|et aperta sunt oculis ejus]], that is, to his divine mind: indeed, all created things are known to the soul of Christ as well. Therefore it is written: [[Ecclus 23:28|the eyes of the Lord are far brighter than the sun, beholding round about all the ways of men|Oculi Domini multo plus lucidiores super solem, circumspicientes omnes vias hominum]]: [[Ecclus 23:29|For all things were known to the Lord God, before they were created|Domino enim Deo antequam crearentur, omnia sunt cognita]]. [[4:13|to whom|Ad quem]], the uncreated Word or Son of God, [[4:13|our speech is|est nobis sermo]] [“sermo”, “word”, also means a reckoning or account], that is, we shall have to stand before him as our judge and render an account[[Rom 14:10||]][[Rom 14:12||]][[2 Cor 5:10||]].

paras.t: Ideo, quum tanta sit potestas, sapientia et eminentia judicis nostri, merito festinare debemus ingredi requiem ejus, ne tanquam ingrati et acediosi condemnemur ab ipso. Propterea hortatur Apostolus: Habentes ergo pontificem magnum, id est summum sacerdotem atque episcopum, qui se ipsum immolavit pro nobis, qui penetravit cœlos, id est, in sua ascensione super omnes cœlos ascendit cum penetratione dimensionum, Jesum Filium Dei naturalem, non adoptivum; teneamus, id est, firmiter observemus et exerceamus, confessionem duplicem, scilicet laudis divinæ et propriæ culpæ, dicentes cum Propheta, Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo: hoc est, Christum laudemus semper, et nostra vitia accusemus.
paras.en: Therefore, since the power, wisdom and eminence of our judge are so great, we rightly ought to hasten to enter his rest, lest we be condemned by him as ungrateful and slothful [“acediosi”, given to accidie, the sloth that is weary of spiritual things]. And so the Apostle exhorts: [[4:14|Having therefore a great high priest|Habentes ergo pontificem magnum]], that is, a supreme priest and bishop[[1 Pet 2:25||]], who offered himself in sacrifice for us[[Eph 5:2||]], [[4:14|that hath passed into the heavens|qui penetravit cœlos]], that is, who in his ascension went up above all the heavens with penetration of dimensions [that is, his body passing through the heavens as through no obstacle][[Acts 1:9||]][[Acts 1:11||]], [[4:14|Jesus the Son of God|Jesum Filium Dei]], Son by nature, not by adoption: [[4:14|let us hold fast|teneamus]], that is, let us firmly keep and practise, [[4:14|our confession|confessionem]], a twofold one, namely of God's praise and of our own fault, saying with the Prophet: [[Ps 9:2|I will give praise to thee, O Lord, with my whole heart|Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo]][[Ps 110:1||]][[Ps 137:1||]] [“confitebor” means both “I will praise” and “I will confess”]: that is, let us praise Christ always, and accuse our own vices.

paras.t: Sic autem fiducialiter agere debemus: Non enim habemus pontificem qui non possit compati, id est condescendere atque clementer succurrere, infirmitatibus nostris; tentatum autem, id est, sed habemus pontificem tentatum a dæmone et Judæis, per omnia principalia genera tentationis, pro similitudine, id est propter similitudinem quam cum aliis hominibus habuit. Ideo enim dæmon et ejus ministri ausi fuerunt Christum tentare, quoniam eum mortalem viderunt. Habitu enim inventus est ut homo. Vel, Pro similitudine, id est pro exemplo, videlicet ut omnibus nobis formam vincendi tentationes proponeret. Absque peccato, id est, tentatio ista nequaquam induxit Christum ad aliquam culpam, nec ipse peccando meruit sic tentari.
