paras.t: Propter quod remissas manus, id est pigras et tepidas affectiones, et soluta genua, id est fortitudinem qua ante stetistis, nunc debilitatam, erigite ad Deum, id est, perficite ut caritatis affectus in vobis flammescant, et ad cœlos vos sublevent. Fortitudo quoque animæ corroboretur in vobis. Corporis etiam manus ac genua debemus ad Deum levare, stando erecti ad eum in oratione ac contemplatione, juxta illud: Levemus corda nostra cum manibus ad Deum in cœlos. Et gressus rectos, id est opera justa, facite pedibus vestris, id est ex interioribus virtutibus animæ, quibus itur ad Deum, videlicet ex fide, spe et caritate, sine quibus nulla actio meritoria est; ut non claudicans, id est instabilis, vagus et in via Domini nutans, quis vestrum erret ab ultimo fine, magis autem sanetur a vulneribus animæ, id est peccatis.
paras.en: [[12:12|Wherefore|Propter quod]] [[12:12|the hands which hang down|remissas manus]], that is, sluggish and lukewarm affections, [[12:12|and the feeble knees|et soluta genua]][[Is 35:3||]], that is, the strength by which you stood before, now weakened, [[12:12|lift up|erigite]] to God: that is, bring it about that the affections of charity blaze up in you and raise you to heaven. Let the strength of the soul also be made firm in you. We ought also to lift up the hands and knees of the body to God, standing upright towards him in prayer and contemplation, according to that saying: [[Lam 3:41|Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to the Lord in the heavens|Levemus corda nostra cum manibus ad Deum in cœlos]] [Denis has *to God* for *to the Lord*]. [[12:13|And make straight steps|Et gressus rectos]], that is, just works, [[12:13|with your feet|facite pedibus vestris]], that is, from the inward virtues of the soul by which one goes to God, namely from faith, hope and charity, without which no action is meritorious; [[12:13|that no one, halting|ut non claudicans]], that is, unstable, wandering and wavering in the way of the Lord, [[12:13|may go out of the way|quis vestrum erret]] from the last end [that is, God, the final end of man], [[12:13|but rather be healed|magis autem sanetur]] of the wounds of the soul, that is, of sins.

paras.t: Pacem, id est tranquillitatem sive concordiam, sequimini, id est, servare curare, cum omnibus proximis, amicis ac æmulis. Quod intelligendum est de vera spiritualique pace. Propter quod et Romanis dictum est: Si fieri potest, cum omnibus hominibus pacem habentes. Et sanctimoniam, id est cordis munditiam, juxta illud: Omni custodia custodi cor tuum. Sine qua pace et sanctimonia nemo videbit Deum in patria. Beati enim pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur. Beati quoque mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt.
paras.en: [[12:14|peace|Pacem]], that is, tranquillity or concord, [[12:14|Follow|sequimini]], that is, take care to keep it, [[12:14|with all men|cum omnibus proximis]], neighbours, friends and rivals alike. This is to be understood of true and spiritual peace. For this reason the Romans too were told: [[Rom 12:18|If it be possible|Si fieri potest]], [[Rom 12:18|have peace with all men|cum omnibus hominibus pacem habentes]]. [[12:14|and holiness|Et sanctimoniam]], that is, cleanness of heart, according to that saying: [[Prov 4:23|With all watchfulness keep thy heart|Omni custodia custodi cor tuum]]. [[12:14|without which|Sine qua]] peace and holiness [[12:14|no man shall see God|nemo videbit Deum]] in the fatherland. For [[Matt 5:9|Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God|Beati enim pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur]]. And also: [[Matt 5:8|Blessed are the clean of heart: they shall see God|Beati quoque mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt]].

paras.t: Contemplantes, id est sollicite præcaventes, ne quis desit gratiæ Dei, id est, ne aliquis vestrum elongetur ac separetur a gratia Dei, quæ omnibus præsto est, dummodo fecerint quod in se est; vel, Ne quis desit gratiæ Dei, id est, ne gratia Dei in vobis imperfecta sit propter negligentiam vestram. Sed potius in ea proficite, ne qua radix amaritudinis, id est, ne aliqua passio vitiosa, pœnalis, seu pœnam promerens, sursum germinans, id est in consensum vel opus prorumpens, impediat gratiam et salutem, et per illam amaritudinem inquinentur, id est, scandalizentur seu perturbentur, multi ex impatientia. Unde in lege præcipitur: Non sit inter vos radix germinans fel et amaritudinem; et Sapiens, Non est sensus ubi abundat amaritudo.
paras.en: [[12:15|Looking diligently|Contemplantes]], that is, carefully guarding beforehand, [[12:15|lest any man be wanting to the grace of God|ne quis desit gratiæ Dei]], that is, lest any of you be drawn away and separated from the grace of God, which is at hand for all, provided they do what is in them [that is, what lies in their power]; or, [[12:15|lest any man be wanting to the grace of God|Ne quis desit gratiæ Dei]], that is, lest the grace of God be imperfect in you through your negligence. But rather make progress in it, [[12:15|lest any root of bitterness|ne qua radix amaritudinis]], that is, lest any vicious passion, penal or deserving of punishment, [[12:15|springing up|sursum germinans]], that is, breaking out into consent or deed, [[12:15|do hinder|impediat]] grace and salvation, [[12:15|and by it|et per illam amaritudinem]] [Denis's text has *by that bitterness*] [[12:15|be defiled|inquinentur]], that is, be scandalized or troubled, [[12:15|many|multi]], through impatience. Hence it is commanded in the law: Let not [[Deut 29:18|a root bringing forth gall and bitterness|radix germinans fel et amaritudinem]] be among you; and the Wise Man: [[Ecclus 21:15|there is no understanding where there is bitterness|Non est sensus ubi abundat amaritudo]] [Denis: *where bitterness abounds*].

paras.t: Ne quis sit fornicator spiritualis, recedendo a fide. Est enim spiritualis fornicatio, qua Deus relinquitur. De qua Propheta: Fornicati sunt a Deo; et in Psalmo, Fornicati sunt in adinventionibus suis. Vel, Ne quis sit fornicator corporalis, illicitum concubitum committendo. Aut profanus, id est penitus irreligiosus, tanquam procul a fano, id est remotus a templo, serviens suo ventri magis quam Deo, ut gulosi; ut Esau, qui propter unam escam, puta lenticulam a Jacob paratam, vendidit ipso Jacob primitiva sua, id est primogenita, scilicet dignitatem primogenitorum, hoc est honorem sacerdotii, prout in Genesi narratur. Primogeniti autem in lege naturæ erant sacerdotes, et speciales vestes habebant, quibus tempore sacerdotii utebantur: habebantque duplicem portionem in hereditate. Jus autem primogenituræ et dignitas sacerdotii, spirituale sunt bonum. Ideo Esau id vendendo, incidit simoniam: non tamen Jacob, quoniam proprie non emit ea: sed sui vexationem redemit, quoniam ex ordinatione divina ei debebantur primogenita.
paras.en: [[12:16|Lest there be any fornicator|Ne quis sit fornicator]] in the spiritual sense, by falling away from the faith. For there is a spiritual fornication, by which God is forsaken. Of it the Prophet says: [[Osee 4:12|they have committed fornication against their God|Fornicati sunt a Deo]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 105:39|they went aside after their own inventions|Fornicati sunt in adinventionibus suis]] [literally, *they committed fornication in their own inventions*]. Or, [[12:16|Lest there be any fornicator|Ne quis sit fornicator]] in the bodily sense, by committing unlawful intercourse. [[12:16|or profane person|Aut profanus]], that is, wholly irreligious, as it were far from the *fanum*, that is, removed from the temple [*pro fano*, "outside the shrine", is the root of *profanus*], serving his own belly rather than God[[Rom 16:18||]], as gluttons do; [[12:16|as Esau who for one mess|ut Esau, qui propter unam escam]], namely the lentils prepared by Jacob, [[12:16|sold|vendidit]] to Jacob himself [[12:16|his first birthright|primitiva sua]], that is, his rights as firstborn, namely the dignity of the firstborn, that is, the honour of the priesthood, as is told in Genesis[[Gen 25:29||]] [the margin gives Gen. xxv, 29–34]. Now in the law of nature the firstborn were priests, and had special vestments, which they wore at the time of their priestly service; and they had a double portion in the inheritance. But the right of the firstborn and the dignity of the priesthood are a spiritual good. Therefore Esau, by selling it, fell into simony; not so Jacob, since he did not properly buy them, but redeemed himself from injury [that is, paid only to obtain what was already his due, which is not simony], since by divine ordinance the birthright was owed to him.

paras.t: Itaque non sit aliquis vestrum fornicator aut profanus ut Esau: Scitote enim quoniam et postea reversus de agro, et Jacob jam benedicto, cupiens Esau hereditare, id est hereditarie possidere vel sumere, benedictionem Isaac, reprobatus est a Deo, et ab impetratione benedictionis prohibitus. Verumtamen in Genesi legitur Isaac benedixisse Esau filio suo, sed non benedictione primogenituræ, quam Esau primo et principaliter postulavit. Non enim invenit pœnitentiæ locum ad recuperandum amissam benedictionem, quanquam cum lacrimis inquisisset eam, id est pœnitentiæ veniam seu benedictionem. Non enim ex amore justitiæ vel vera contritione profluxerunt lacrimæ illæ, sed ex temporalis damni mœrore, vel indignatione sive rancore. Simili modo de Antiocho scribitur: Orabat scelestus Dominum, a quo non esset misericordiam consecuturus. Neminem tamen Deus repellit, si recta intentione convertatur ad eum. Quis enim invocavit Deum, et despexit eum?
paras.en: So let none of you be a [[12:16|fornicator or profane person, as Esau|fornicator aut profanus ut Esau]]: [[12:17|For know ye that afterwards|Scitote enim quoniam et postea]], when he had come back from the field, Jacob being already blessed[[Gen 27:30||]] [the margin gives Gen. xxvii, 30–37], Esau, [[12:17|when he desired to inherit|cupiens Esau hereditare]], that is, to possess or take as an inheritance, [[12:17|the benediction|benedictionem Isaac]] of Isaac, [[12:17|he was rejected|reprobatus est]] by God, and kept from obtaining the blessing. Yet we read in Genesis that Isaac blessed his son Esau[[Gen 27:39||]] [the margin gives Ibid. 34, 40; Isaac's blessing of Esau is Gen 27:39–40], but not with the blessing of the firstborn, which Esau had asked for first and chiefly. [[12:17|For he found no place of repentance|Non enim invenit pœnitentiæ locum]] to recover the blessing he had lost, [[12:17|although with tears he had sought it|quanquam cum lacrimis inquisisset eam]], that is, pardon through repentance, or the blessing. For those tears did not flow from love of justice or from true contrition, but from grief at a temporal loss, or from indignation or rancour. In like manner it is written of Antiochus: [[2 Mach 9:13|this wicked man prayed to the Lord, of whom he was not like to obtain mercy|Orabat scelestus Dominum, a quo non esset misericordiam consecuturus]]. Yet God repels no one, if he turns to him with a right intention. For [[Ecclus 2:12|who hath called upon him, and he despised him|Quis enim invocavit Deum, et despexit eum]]? [the margin gives Ecclus. xii, 12; the words are Ecclus 2:12]

paras.t: Deinde assignat Apostolus rationem, cur nullus deesse debet gratiæ Dei: eo quod nova lex sit lex pietatis, amoris et gratiæ; vetus autem lex, erat lex timoris, rigoris et mortis. Non enim accessistis ad tractabilem, id est palpabilem, et accessibilem motu corporeo, ignem, qualis fuit ignis ardens in monte Sinai tempore dationis legis antiquæ. Nec accessistis et ad turbinem, id est ventum vehementem qui fit cum grandine et pluvia, et caliginem, id est ignis tenebrositatem, et procellam, id est ingentem tempestatem, et tubæ sonitum, qualis audiebatur in monte Sinai, et vocem verborum, id est vocem angeli loquentis cum Moyse. De his namque legitur: Ceperunt audiri tonitrua, et micare fulgura, et nubes densissima operuit montem; clangor quoque buccinæ vehementius perstrepebat, totusque mons Sinai fumigabat. In his quippe terribilibus data est lex, ad significandum ejus rigorem. Quam procellam et vocem qui audierunt, videlicet filii Israel perterriti, excusaverunt se, suam infirmitatem allegando, ne eis fieret verbum immediate ab angelo loquente in persona Dei, sed a Moyse, dicentes: Loquere tu nobis, et audiemus; non loquatur nobis Dominus, ne forte moriamur. Quid enim est omnis caro, ut audiat vocem Dei loquentis de medio ignis? Ideo subditur: Non enim portabant, id est, sustinere et audire non poterant, quod dicebatur, id est verbum angeli cum Moyse terribiliter loquentis. Et si bestia tetigerit montem, lapidabitur, id est, hoc quoque dictum fuit a Deo per angelum et per Moysen ad populum, quod si bestia tetigerit montem Sinai, transeundo ultra terminum præfixum, lapidibus obrueretur. Hoc dictum fuit etiam de hominibus. Et ita terribile erat quod videbatur in monte Sinai. Moyses dixit: Exterritus sum corde, et tremebundus in corpore. Multo magis alii formidabant. Hoc Moyses non legitur dixisse in datione legis; sed in visione rubi ardentis ostendit se territum, abscondendo faciem suam, quoniam non audebat respicere contra Dominum.
paras.en: Then the Apostle gives the reason why no one ought to be wanting to the grace of God: because the new law is a law of loving-kindness, love and grace, while the old law was a law of fear, of rigour and of death. [[12:18|For you are not come|Non enim accessistis]] to something [[12:18|that might be touched|ad tractabilem]], that is, palpable, and approachable by bodily movement, a [[12:18|fire|ignem]], such as was the fire burning on mount Sinai at the time the old law was given [Denis's text reads *ad tractabilem et accessibilem ignem*, "to a fire that may be touched and approached", without *montem*, "mountain", and with *accessibilem* for *accensibilem*, "burning"]. Nor are you come [[12:18|and a whirlwind|et ad turbinem]], that is, a violent wind that comes with hail and rain, [[12:18|and darkness|et caliginem]], that is, the murkiness of the fire, [[12:18|and storm|et procellam]], that is, a mighty tempest, [[12:19|And the sound of a trumpet|et tubæ sonitum]], such as was heard on mount Sinai, [[12:19|and the voice of words|et vocem verborum]], that is, the voice of the angel speaking with Moses. For of these we read: [[Ex 19:16|thunders began to be heard, and lightning to flash, and a very thick cloud to cover the mount, and the noise of the trumpet sounded exceeding loud|Ceperunt audiri tonitrua, et micare fulgura, et nubes densissima operuit montem; clangor quoque buccinæ vehementius perstrepebat]], and [[Ex 19:18|all Mount Sinai was on a smoke|totusque mons Sinai fumigabat]]. For the law was given amid these terrors, to signify its rigour. [[12:19|which|Quam]], the storm and the voice, [[12:19|they that|qui audierunt]] heard, namely the terrified children of Israel, [[12:19|had excused themselves|excusaverunt se]], pleading their weakness, [[12:19|that the word might not be spoken to them|ne eis fieret verbum]] directly by the angel speaking in the person of God, but by Moses, saying: [[Ex 20:19|Speak thou to us, and we will hear: let not the Lord speak to us, lest we die|Loquere tu nobis, et audiemus; non loquatur nobis Dominus, ne forte moriamur]]. For [[Deut 5:26|What is all flesh, that it should hear the voice of the living God, who speaketh out of the midst of the fire|Quid enim est omnis caro, ut audiat vocem Dei loquentis de medio ignis?]]? Therefore is added: [[12:20|For they did not endure|Non enim portabant]], that is, they could not bear and hear, [[12:20|that which was said|quod dicebatur]], that is, the word of the angel speaking terribly with Moses. [[12:20|and if so much as a beast shall touch the mount, it shall be stoned|Et si bestia tetigerit montem, lapidabitur]], that is, this too was said by God, through the angel and through Moses, to the people: that if a beast touched mount Sinai, passing beyond the boundary set, it should be overwhelmed with stones. This was said of men too. [[12:21|And so terrible was that which was seen|Et ita terribile erat quod videbatur]] on mount Sinai. [[12:21|Moses said: I am frighted, and tremble|Moyses dixit: Exterritus sum corde, et tremebundus in corpore]] [Denis's text adds *in heart* and *in body*]. Much more were the others afraid. We do not read that Moses said this at the giving of the law; but at the vision of the burning bush he showed that he was afraid, hiding his face, because [[Ex 3:6|he durst not look at God|non audebat respicere contra Dominum]].

paras.t: Per ista ostendit Apostolus, quod non sumus sub lege timoris, sed amoris et gratiæ: ideo gratia nobis parata est. Unde subjungitur: Sed accessistis per Baptismatis susceptionem, ad Sion montem, id est Ecclesiam militantem, Deum in alto contemplantem. Sion enim interpretatur speculatio. Ecclesia vero mons dicitur, propter vitæ et gratiæ eminentiam. Accessistis quoque per spem ad civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem, id est Ecclesiam triumphantem, […] millium angelorum frequentiam, id est frequentem multitudinem. Nunc enim speratis pertingere ad societatem angelorum, qui pene innumerabiles sunt, juxta illud: Millia millium ministrabant ei, et decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei; et in Job: Numquid est numerus militum ejus? et super quem non surgit lumen ipsius? Et ad ecclesiam primitivorum, id est congregationem et societatem Apostolorum, et aliorum qui primo crediderunt in Christum, qui conscripti sunt in cœlis, id est in libro vitæ, quatenus ad cœlestem gloriam perducantur, quemadmodum dixit eis Salvator: Gaudete et exsultate, quia nomina vestra scripta sunt in cœlis.
paras.en: By these things the Apostle shows that we are not under a law of fear, but of love and grace: and so grace is made ready for us. Hence he adds: [[12:22|But you are come|Sed accessistis]], by the receiving of Baptism, [[12:22|to mount Sion|ad Sion montem]], that is, the Church militant, which contemplates God on high. For Sion is interpreted *watching* [*speculatio*, a looking out from a height]. And the Church is called a mountain because of the eminence of its life and grace. You are come also by hope [[12:22|to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem|ad civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem]], that is, the Church triumphant, […] [[12:22|the company of many thousands of angels|millium angelorum frequentiam]], that is, a thronging multitude. For now you hope to attain to the fellowship of the angels, who are almost innumerable, according to that saying: [[Dan 7:10|thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times a hundred thousand stood before him|Millia millium ministrabant ei, et decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei]]; and in Job: [[Job 25:3|Is there any numbering of his soldiers? and upon whom shall not his light arise?|Numquid est numerus militum ejus? et super quem non surgit lumen ipsius?]]? [[12:23|And to the church of the firstborn|Et ad ecclesiam primitivorum]], that is, the congregation and fellowship of the Apostles, and of others who first believed in Christ, [[12:23|who are written in the heavens|qui conscripti sunt in cœlis]], that is, in the book of life, so that they may be brought to heavenly glory; as the Saviour said to them: [[Luke 10:20|rejoice in this, that your names are written in heaven|Gaudete et exsultate, quia nomina vestra scripta sunt in cœlis]] [Denis's wording: *Rejoice and be glad, for your names are written in heaven*].

paras.t: Accessistis quoque per fidem et caritatem et ad judicem omnium Deum, id est ad Deum Patrem, cui ex propria auctoritate primarie competit judicare. Unde ait Salvator: Ego non judico quemquam; est qui quærat et judicet. Tamen prosecutio judicii collata est Christo homini. Et spiritum justorum perfectorum, id est ad Spiritum Sanctum, qui facit atque inhabitat justos et perfectos, tanquam familiaris cum eis; et testamenti novi mediatorem Jesum, id est ad Christum Filium Dei, qui est medius dator evangelicæ legis, inter Deum Trinitatem et homines medians, pacemque faciens, et sanguinis adspersionem, id est ad participationem efficaciæ seu fructus ac meriti sanguinis Christi, per quem mundamur a pœna et culpa in Baptismo, in quo adspergimur merito sanguinis Christi, id est infusione gratiæ: adspersionem, inquam, melius loquentem quam loquitur effusio sanguinis Abel. Sanguis enim Christi clamat et efficit pacem ac veniam; sanguis vero Abel, vindictam et damnationem.
paras.en: You are come also, by faith and charity, [[12:23|and to God the judge of all|et ad judicem omnium Deum]], that is, to God the Father, to whom it belongs primarily, by his own authority, to judge. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 8:15|I judge not any man|Ego non judico quemquam]]; [[John 8:50|there is one that seeketh and judgeth|est qui quærat et judicet]]. Yet the carrying out of judgment has been committed to Christ as man. [[12:23|and to the spirits of the just made perfect|Et spiritum justorum perfectorum]] [Denis reads *spiritum*, singular, "the spirit"], that is, to the Holy Spirit, who makes the just and perfect and dwells in them as one of their household; [[12:24|And to Jesus the mediator of the new testament|et testamenti novi mediatorem Jesum]], that is, to Christ the Son of God, who is the giver in the middle [*medius dator*, a play on *mediator*] of the law of the Gospel, mediating between God the Trinity and men[[Eph 2:14||]], and [[Eph 2:15|making peace|pacemque faciens]] [the margin gives Eph. iv, 14, 15; the words are Eph 2:14–15], [[12:24|and to the sprinkling of blood|et sanguinis adspersionem]], that is, to a share in the efficacy, or the fruit and merit, of the blood of Christ, by which we are cleansed from punishment and guilt in Baptism, in which we are sprinkled by the merit of Christ's blood, that is, by the infusion of grace: a sprinkling, I say, [[12:24|which speaketh better than that of Abel|melius loquentem quam loquitur effusio sanguinis Abel]] [Denis: *than the shedding of Abel's blood speaks*]. For the blood of Christ cries out for peace and pardon and brings them about; but the blood of Abel, for vengeance and damnation[[Gen 4:10||]].

paras.t: Videte ne recusetis loquentem, id est, ne Christum in Evangelio vos exhortantem audire spernatis. Si enim, id est quia, illi rebelles Judæi non effugerunt debitam pœnam, recusantes, id est audire contemnentes, eum qui super terram loquebatur eis, id est Moysen vel angelum loquentem in monte Sinai; multo magis nos, qui de cœlis loquentem nobis, id est Christum in cœlo jam residentem et nobis in Evangelio loquentem, avertimus, id est, per inobedientiam a cordibus nostris repellimus, non evademus pœnas condignas.
paras.en: [[12:25|See that you refuse him not that speaketh|Videte ne recusetis loquentem]], that is, lest you scorn to hear Christ exhorting you in the Gospel. [[12:25|For if|Si enim]], that is, since, those rebellious Jews [[12:25|escaped not|non effugerunt]] the punishment due, [[12:25|who refused|recusantes]], that is, scorned to hear, [[12:25|him that spoke upon earth|eum qui super terram loquebatur]] to them, that is, Moses, or the angel speaking on mount Sinai; [[12:25|much more shall not we|multo magis nos]], [[12:25|that turn away from him that speaketh to us from heaven|qui de cœlis loquentem nobis]], that is, from Christ, now dwelling in heaven and speaking to us in the Gospel, [[12:25|turn away|avertimus]], that is, drive him from our hearts by disobedience, escape the punishment we deserve.

paras.t: Cujus Christi vox, id est potestas et sermo, movit terram, id est montem Sinai, qui tremere videbatur, tunc, quum lex dabatur. Vox enim angeli movientis tunc terram, dicitur vox Christi, quoniam in persona Dei, et per consequens in persona Christi loquebatur, quum ipse sit verus Deus. Unde et ipse ait: Creditis in Deum, et in me credite. Nunc autem, id est pro tempore novi testamenti, Christus repromittit, dicens: Adhuc semel, præter id scilicet quod ante feci in monte Sinai, hoc est in primo meo adventu: et ego movebo non solum terram, quæ mota est tempore passionis, sed et cœlum aerium, quod insolito more motum est, angelis tempore nativitatis Christi apparentibus, et novo sidere radiante de cœlo, Christo quoque cum Sanctis innumerabilibus ascendente in cœlum. Quemadmodum autem per motum terræ intelligi potest motio et admiratio hominum; sic per motum cœli intelligi potest ascensus atque descensus et admiratio angelorum, qui in primo Christi adventu frequenter apparuerunt, et vehementer mirati sunt de mysteriis Christi, dicentes in ascensione: Quis est iste qui venit de Edom? et, Quis est iste Rex gloriæ?
paras.en: [[12:26|Whose voice|Cujus Christi vox]], Christ's, that is, his power and word, [[12:26|moved the earth|movit terram]], that is, mount Sinai, which was seen to tremble[[Ex 19:16||]][[Ex 19:18||]], [[12:26|then|tunc]], when the law was given. For the voice of the angel who then moved the earth is called the voice of Christ, since he spoke in the person of God, and consequently in the person of Christ, since Christ is true God. Hence he himself says: [[John 14:1|You believe in God: believe also in me|Creditis in Deum, et in me credite]]. [[12:26|but now|Nunc autem]], that is, for the time of the new testament, Christ [[12:26|promiseth, saying|repromittit, dicens]]: [[12:26|Yet once more|Adhuc semel]][[Agg 2:7||]], besides, namely, what I did before on mount Sinai, that is, in my first coming: [[12:26|and I will move, not only the earth|et ego movebo non solum terram]], which was moved at the time of the passion[[Matt 27:51||]], [[12:26|but heaven also|sed et cœlum]], the heaven of the air, which was moved in an unwonted manner when angels appeared at the time of Christ's birth[[Luke 2:13||]], and a new star shone from heaven[[Matt 2:2||]], and when Christ, too, ascended into heaven with innumerable Saints[[Acts 1:9||]]. And as by the moving of the earth may be understood the stirring and wonder of men, so by the moving of heaven may be understood the ascending and descending and the wonder of the angels, who often appeared at Christ's first coming and greatly marvelled at the mysteries of Christ, saying at the ascension: [[Is 63:1|Who is this that cometh from Edom|Quis est iste qui venit de Edom]]? and, [[Ps 23:8|Who is this King of Glory|Quis est iste Rex gloriæ]][[Ps 23:10||]]?

paras.t: Consequenter exponit quædam verba auctoritatis inductæ. Quod autem, Adhuc semel, dicit, id est, per hoc quod Propheta hæc duo connectit, Adhuc, et, Semel, declarat mobilium, id est variabilium rerum, scilicet elementorum et orbium, translationem, id est corruptionem, quantum ad statum et formas quasdam accidentales, seu transmutationem in meliorem statum, tanquam factorum, id est a Deo creatorum. Idcirco, quum sint a Deo creata, possunt ab eo transferri in alium statum. Quod erit in die judicii. Ut maneant ea quæ sunt, immobilia, id est, hæc eadem in melius transmutata, in æternum perseverent: quia post diem judicii cessabit generatio et corruptio in rebus corporeis.
paras.en: Next he explains certain words of the authority brought in. [[12:27|And in that he saith: Yet once more|Quod autem, Adhuc semel, dicit]], that is, by the Prophet's joining these two, *Yet* and *once*, [[12:27|he signifieth|declarat]], [[12:27|of the moveable things|mobilium]], that is, of changeable things, namely the elements and the spheres, [[12:27|the translation|translationem]], that is, their corruption as to their state and certain accidental forms, or their change into a better state, [[12:27|as made|tanquam factorum]], that is, created by God. Therefore, since they were created by God, they can be translated by him into another state. This will be at the day of judgment. [[12:27|that those things may remain which are immoveable|Ut maneant ea quæ sunt, immobilia]], that is, that these same things, changed for the better, may endure for ever: because after the day of judgment generation and corruption will cease in bodily things.

paras.t: Vel sic: Quod autem, Adhuc semel, dicit, id est, per hoc quod de tempore gratiæ loquitur, declarat mobilium translationem, id est cæremonialium veteris legis cessationem, tanquam factorum, id est quasi ad tempus institutorum a Deo, non ut semper durarent: ut maneant ea quæ sunt immobilia, id est, status, ritus, et sacramenta novæ legis usque ad finem sæculi perseverent.
paras.en: Or thus: [[12:27|And in that he saith: Yet once more|Quod autem, Adhuc semel, dicit]], that is, by speaking of the time of grace, [[12:27|he signifieth the translation of the moveable things|declarat mobilium translationem]], that is, the ceasing of the ceremonies of the old law, [[12:27|as made|tanquam factorum]], that is, as instituted by God for a time, not to last for ever: [[12:27|that those things may remain which are immoveable|ut maneant ea quæ sunt immobilia]], that is, that the state, rites and sacraments of the new law may endure until the end of the world.

paras.t: Itaque regnum immobile, id est ecclesia, suscipientes, modo in spe, suscepturi illud in re, habemus gratiam gratum facientem, per quam serviamus, observando præcepta, placentes Deo, id est opera meritoria perpetrantes: serviamus, inquam, cum metu, in quantum est Domi[…]
paras.en: [[12:28|Therefore|Itaque]] [[12:28|an immoveable kingdom|regnum immobile]], that is, the Church, [[12:28|receiving|suscipientes]] now in hope, as we shall receive it hereafter in reality, [[12:28|we have grace|habemus gratiam]] that makes us pleasing [*gratia gratum faciens*, that is, sanctifying grace], [[12:28|whereby let us serve|per quam serviamus]] by keeping the commandments, [[12:28|pleasing God|placentes Deo]], that is, doing meritorious works: let us serve, I say, [[12:28|with fear|cum metu]], in so far as he is […]
